articles.title: 'Play according to the situation': Aaryavir Sehwag reveals Virat Kohli inspiration after finishing as U19 Asia Cup's top run-scorer
articles.summary: Carrying the Sehwag surname comes with its own expectations, but young India batter Aaryavir Sehwag is keen to carve out his identity by focusing on what
articles.body: Carrying the Sehwag surname comes with its own expectations, but young India batter Aaryavir Sehwag is keen to carve out his identity by focusing on what the team needs rather than sticking to a particular batting style. The 17-year-old has found inspiration in Virat Kohli, whose ability to adapt to match situations and take responsibility has shaped his own approach to batting.Aaryavir enjoyed a memorable campaign at the ACC Under-19 Asia Cup in Oman, finishing as the tournament's leading run-scorer with 361 runs in five matches. His tally included a century and three half-centuries, performances that earned him the Player of the Tournament award as India lifted their ninth title with a thrilling one-wicket victory over Pakistan in the final.The youngster's ability to adapt to different conditions and build his innings according to the team's requirements stood out throughout the competition. Speaking to JioStar, Aaryavir opened up about his admiration for Kohli and explained why he does not want to be labelled as a particular type of batter.'I am a huge Virat Kohli fan': Aaryavir on his batting philosophyAaryavir said Kohli's approach to batting has inspired him to assess situations carefully and adjust his game according to the team's requirements. Rather than identifying himself as an aggressive stroke-maker or an accumulator, the youngster wants to remain flexible and play according to the demands of the match."I don't label myself as a stroke player or any kind of player. I just want to play according to the situation. As I've said earlier, I am a huge Virat Kohli fan, and I want to do what the team requires and needs at that time. I'm glad that I could play the way I did," he told JioStar.Aaryavir Sehwag recalls challenging conditions during 160-run knock against UAEAaryavir smashed 160 off 168 deliveries, including 17 fours and seven sixes, to help India post 309/7 against the UAE. India eventually secured a 70-run victory to book their place in the semifinals. Reflecting on the innings, the youngster revealed that negotiating the initial seam movement was a key part of his plan. However, the pitch also offered unexpected turn, making batting challenging even after the opening overs."Initially, those 10 to 15 overs have always been a challenge in Oman throughout the Asia Cup. In those first 10 to 15 overs, the plan was to see off the seam movement, and after that, shockingly, there was turn as well in that match against UAE. It was a strange kind of wicket, but I'm glad that I could spend a good amount of time on that wicket and once I got set, I just kept batting, and the runs kept coming," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: India boycott trophy ceremony after Pakistan handed Blind Asia Cup title following washout
articles.summary: MUMBAI: A massive controversy erupted on Friday after Pakistan were declared the winners of the Men's Blind Cricket Asia Cup 2026 in Dhaka, despite the
articles.body: MUMBAI: A massive controversy erupted on Friday after Pakistan were declared the winners of the Men's Blind Cricket Asia Cup 2026 in Dhaka, despite the much-anticipated final against India being completely washed out.The match referee, Tamim from Bangladesh, declared Pakistan the champions on the basis of their superior Net Run Rate (NRR) in the league stage. However, the Indian team has disputed the decision, claiming that this clause was never mentioned in the tournament's playing conditions provided to them.India subsequently boycotted the trophy presentation ceremony and rejected the match referee's decision to award the title to Pakistan.India had earlier lost to Pakistan in the league stage in a thrilling last-over encounter."It's completely unfair. It's been raining here in Dhaka since yesterday because of a cyclone. The final was supposed to start at 11:30 am. However, the match didn't start at all. As per match rules, we were at the ground (ABG Sports City ground in Dhaka). However, at 4:15 pm, the match was abandoned due to rain and the match referee declared Pakistan the winner due to a better Net Run Rate in the league stage."This rule was never mentioned to us in the playing conditions provided to us, or mentioned in the meetings of the match referee with the captains a day before the tournament began. As per the playing conditions, if the match had been tied and a Super Over was played and that also remained tied, then the winner being decided on the Net Run Rate rule would've been applicable."Nowhere in the history of cricket has one team been declared the winner despite the final being abandoned without a ball being bowled! Neither the ICC nor the MCC rules have such a rule in place in case the final of a tournament is washed out. It's clear that the laws have been twisted to declare Pakistan the tournament winners. Both the teams should have been declared joint winners, or the final should've been played on a reserve day," Dhiraj Sequeira, manager of the Indian blind team, told TOI from Dhaka."We appealed against the decision to award Pakistan the trophy to the technical committee of the tournament, but they too rejected our appeal, despite two members of the panel being in favour of our appeal. Consequently, we decided to boycott the presentation ceremony, after consulting CABI," Sequeira added."CABI is not too hopeful of getting any 'justice' from the World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC), as its president is Pakistan's Syed Sultan Shah, who is also the president/chairman of the Pakistan Blind Cricket Council.""Pakistan made the match referee declare the result in their favour, despite the final being totally washed out? How is this possible? I feel very ashamed about it. It's a dark day in the history of blind cricket. A trophy has been awarded to Pakistan, which they don't deserve to win at all. They should feel ashamed to carry this trophy."The organisers never conveyed this rule to us previously, and neither does such a rule of declaring a tournament winner exist. This is a self-made, last-minute rule. We've not accepted this result. Hence, we boycotted the presentation ceremony. I am completely disappointed."We would've been happy if they had beaten India in the final. We don't care. Winning and losing is always a part of the game. In the league match, they defeated us on the last ball (players from both sides shook hands too). That's fine. It was such a wonderful match. We were very happy about it. We accepted it. If they had played and won, we would have gracefully accepted the result," Mahantesh GK, president of the Cricket Association for the Blind in India (CABI), told TOI."We (India's men's and women's blind teams) are considering abstaining from playing against Pakistan in global tournaments (for the blind) from now on," he asserted.In a strongly worded statement issued on Friday, CABI condemned the decision to declare Pakistan the sole winners of the Men's Blind Cricket Asia Cup 2026 after the final against India was washed out due to rain.CABI categorically rejected the decision, maintaining that India and Pakistan should be recognised as joint winners.According to CABI, Section 27 of the tournament's technical regulations deals specifically with a tied final, with both sentences referring to that situation. CABI said it raised this interpretation with the World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC) Technical Committee, which initially agreed to declare both teams joint winners.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Selectors are making a blunder': Krishnamachari Srikkanth questions India's handling of Vaibhav Sooryavanshi
articles.summary: Former India captain and chief selector Krishnamachari Srikkanth has launched a strong criticism of the selectors and team management over their handling
articles.body: Former India captain and chief selector Krishnamachari Srikkanth has launched a strong criticism of the selectors and team management over their handling of teenage batting sensation Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, insisting that the youngster deserves a consistent run in the Indian side. Srikkanth believes the 15-year-old has the potential to become a match-winner across formats and even play a significant role in reviving Test cricket globally.Speaking at the sports event on Friday, Srikkanth said the selectors and team management were making a mistake by not providing Sooryavanshi with enough opportunities.'They are discouraging him': Srikkanth slams selectors over Sooryavanshi's treatmentSrikkanth questioned the decision to pick Sooryavanshi for one match and then leave him out for several games, stressing that the youngster needed sustained opportunities to prove his abilities."What they (selectors and team management) are doing with him is not right. They are not encouraging him; they are discouraging him, which is not done. These guys are making a blunder. They play him for one match, they don't play him for five matches. That's not done. Sad," Srikkanth said at the event.'Test cricket revival happens all over the world': Srikkanth backs Sooryavanshi's potentialGoing a step further, Srikkanth suggested that Sooryavanshi's success in the longest format could generate renewed interest in Test cricket, not just in India but across the cricketing world."If Sooryavanshi clicks in Test cricket, a Test cricket revival happens all over the world, not just for India, all over the world. Today in New Zealand, when he was playing the T20 matches, people came all the way -- a full crowd -- to watch Sooryavanshi bat. Wherever he goes, everybody comes to watch Sooryavanshi bat," he said.He called on the selectors to show faith in the youngster and give him a sustained run instead of making frequent changes to his selection."This boy has done so brilliantly for you -- let him play all the matches. Do you mean to say he is not good enough to play Test or One Day cricket? He is 100 per cent sure to play good One Day cricket. Give him 20 innings, tell him he won't get dropped -- you do whatever you want. That boy will win five to seven matches single-handedly for you."And if he scores in Test cricket, the whole world will start reviving Test cricket everywhere, in any part of the world," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Asia Cup Rising Stars: India A crush Nepal by 306 runs after bowling them out for 26
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India A registered a staggering 306-run victory over Nepal in their opening match of the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, producing a
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India A registered a staggering 306-run victory over Nepal in their opening match of the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, producing a dominant all-round performance at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium in Doha.After posting 332/9 in 50 overs, India A's bowlers delivered a sensational performance to dismiss Nepal for just 26 in 11.3 overs. Nepal's total is the fourth-lowest in List A cricket history.Tilak Varma, Kushagra power India A to 332Batting first, India A recovered from a few early setbacks through a magnificent 206-run partnership between captain Tilak Varma and wicketkeeper-batter Kumar Kushagra.Kushagra smashed 117 off 102 deliveries, including 10 fours and five sixes, while Varma scored 107 off 113 balls, hitting six fours and four sixes. Both batters registered centuries to put India A in a commanding position.Suryansh Shedge provided the finishing fireworks with an unbeaten 36 off just 14 balls, featuring four sixes and a boundary, as India A finished on 332/9. For Nepal, Lalit Rajbanshi and Sandeep Lamichhane picked up three wickets each.Rana and Prince trigger historic Nepal collapseNepal's chase never got going as Harshit Rana and Prince Yadav exploited the conditions brilliantly, generating considerable swing and seam movement.Returning from injury, Rana looked in excellent rhythm, striking in the opening over by trapping Arjun Kumal lbw for a duck. Prince then dismissed Deepak Dumre and bowled Basir Ahamad as Nepal slipped to 1-3 inside two overs.The collapse continued as Rana and Prince kept finding breakthroughs. Rana finished with four wickets for 16 runs in six overs, while Prince produced a sensational five-wicket haul, conceding just six runs in five overs.Shahbaz Ahmed claimed the final wicket, stumping Nandan Yadav for 2, as Nepal were bundled out for 26. The result sealed a remarkable 306-run win for India A.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'We didn't have our full-strength team here': Nepal captain Lamichhane after 306-run defeat to India A
articles.summary: Nepal captain Sandeep Lamichhane admitted his side were completely outplayed by India A, while pointing to the absence of several first-choice players as
articles.body: Nepal captain Sandeep Lamichhane admitted his side were completely outplayed by India A, while pointing to the absence of several first-choice players as a challenge ahead of their Asia Cup Rising Stars campaign."We were outplayed today. Credit goes to the way the Indian team carried their momentum. We had a good start with the ball, but they utilised their skills. Credit to Tilak and Kumar for the way they handled the pressure," Lamichhane said after the match.The Nepal skipper also revealed that the team were dealing with availability issues, with several players arriving in Doha on the morning of the match due to the ongoing Nepal Premier League (NPL) back home."We didn't have our full-strength team here. A few of the players arrived this morning. NPL is going on back home. We somehow had to manage and put some new faces for this tournament. It was really a hard task for us to manage everything," he added.Despite the heavy defeat, Lamichhane remained confident about Nepal's prospects in the upcoming matches, insisting that the team understood where they had fallen short."But we all are going in the right direction. We are still fully confident about how we're going to approach the upcoming games. We know where we lacked today," he said, reiterating that India A deserved full credit for their performance.Rana, Prince Yadav dismantle Nepal for 26India A’s pace duo of Harshit Rana and Prince Yadav produced a sensational bowling performance to bundle out Nepal for just 26 in 11.3 overs, sealing a massive 306-run victory in their opening match of the Asia Cup Rising Stars 50-over tournament on Friday.Chasing a daunting target of 333, Nepal’s innings fell apart from the outset. Rana struck in the third ball, trapping Arjun Kamal leg-before without scoring, and the wickets continued to tumble. Nepal were reduced to 17 for five by the seventh over as the Indian pacers exploited the pace and swing on offer.Rana finished with impressive figures of 4/16, while Prince was even more devastating, claiming 5/6. The pair accounted for nine of Nepal’s 10 wickets, leaving India A skipper Tilak Varma with no need to use his other bowling options.Left-arm spinner Shahbaz Ahmed picked up the remaining wicket. Nepal’s batting collapse was complete when they were bowled out for 26, with none of their batters managing to reach double figures.Earlier, centuries from Varma (107) and Kumar Kushagra (117) had powered India A to 332 for nine.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: India A produced a record-breaking performance in their opening match of the ACC Men’s Asia Cup Rising Stars 2026, thrashing Nepal by 306 runs at the West End Park International Cricket Stadium on Friday. articles.title: James Anderson: England legend loses Italia T10 league debut for Napoli Knights in first match since Lancashire exit
articles.summary: James Anderson was released by Lancashire at the end of the County Championship season and has joined Surrey in 2027; Anderson is among the players in action for Napoli Knights, a T10 franchise league in Italy
articles.body:
Anderson is co-owner of Napoli Knights, with the 44-year-old's appearance his first since being released by boyhood club Lancashire at the end of the season.

Napoli Knights are one of six teams in the nine-day tournament at Roma Cricket Ground, running until November 28, with Anderson's side restricted to 73-9 after losing the toss and batting first.

Anderson finished nought not out from one delivery faced, scampering a bye from the final ball of the innings, before taking 0-14 from two overs during Rome Gladiators' successful chase.

England's history-making Test bowler conceded just three from a tight opening over of Rome's chase, before being hit down the ground by Singh for a maximum - during an 11-run over - when returning for a second stint later in the innings.

Anthony Mosca fired an unbeaten 45 from 27 deliveries and Jaspreet Singh ended 15 not out from nine, as Rome Gladiators claimed a five-wicket win with two balls remaining.

Wayne Madsen, captaining the Napoli Knights: "It's fantastic to have Jimmy [Anderson] here. He's inspirational to so many of us.

"To be playing with him, and for him to share his knowledge with this group, is amazing. I think, as we've seen, he has still got the skill to go out there and perform at the top level."

Napoli Knights have further matches against Brescia Lions (Saturday), Venice Livewire (Sunday), Milan Icons (Monday) and Bologna Hurricanes (TBC).

Anderson has joined Surrey ahead of the 2027 season in the Rothesay County Championship, having been left "sad" and "quite shocked" by his contract not being extended by Lancashire .

Upon the announcement of his move to the Kia Oval, Anderson said: "It's an honour to join a club like Surrey and I can't wait to start a new chapter in my career. I still feel like I have a lot to offer, taking wickets, trying to help the team win games of cricket.

"I also think that I can bring a lot to the team off the field and help those young players who are looking to develop their skillset and go on and represent their country."

Anderson, who turns 45 in July of next year, will get the opportunity to add to his haul of 1,193 first-class wickets and perhaps more silverware to a glittering CV.

articles.title: Josh Hazlewood defends Pat Cummins over 'Sandpapergate' and backs Australia's Test captain to continue after "pile-on"
articles.summary: Australia captain Pat Cummins has been scrutinised after Cameron Bancroft's damning account of the 2018 sandpaper scandal; Josh Hazlewood defended Cummins in a new interview and questioned how the Test team would react if he was forced to step away as captain
articles.body:
Cameron Bancroft plunged Australian cricket into further turmoil with a 4,000-word statement, backing claims "the whole team" knew about the plot and contradicting strong denials Cummins offered in his press conference a few days earlier.

Cummins had branded Khawaja's testimony "complete and utter nonsense" and "100 per cent wrong", leading Bancroft to go public with his story, while Australia's Test captain has had his future speculated after how he has handled the incident.

"It feels like it's been a bit of a pile on the last few days [at Cummins] from different people," Hazlewood told CodeSports . "I want to back Pat [Cummins] and everything he said in his press conference last week, everything he's done for the last five or six years in particular as captain.

"To get the group where it is now and in a position where something like that [sandpaper] is never going to happen again - I think is just a remarkable job. He's a great leader. If you went around and asked everyone in the team, you'd hear the same response.

"If we turned up for the first Test and he wasn't the captain and it was someone else, honestly, I don't know how that would go."

Australia are next in Test action when they face New Zealand in a four-match series, beginning on December 9 in Perth, where Hazlewood would consider whether to feature if Cummins was no longer captain.

"I'd have to be put in that position to make a decision, but you'd have to think about it, yeah," Hazlewood added.

Hazlewood denies involvement in sandpaper plan

Bancroft, Warner and then-captain Steve Smith all served bans for their role in the ball-tampering plot, while Hazelwood remains adamant on his position that the bowlers did not know about the use of sandpaper.

"We were interviewed straight after [Cape Town] and I trust what I said in that two-three hour interrogation more than anything because it was in the day or two after," Hazlewood explained.

"It was fresh in my mind at that point. Two things stand out for me from what's been said. Was I an architect in the plan to tamper with the ball with sandpaper? And was I aware sandpaper or foreign substances being used on the field?

"The answer is no. When it boils down to it, I think those two points are crucial."

On whether he noticed a change in ball condition during that Test, Hazlewood said: "I never remember looking at the ball and going, 'wow, this is not natural deterioration'. And obviously the umpires didn't either."

Former England captain Michael Atherton said on the Sky Sports Cricket Podcas t he does not expect Cummins to resign from his role as Test skipper.

"He's obviously got a lot of credit in the bank in terms of performance as captain, having transformed the culture and kept Australia at the top of the tree, if you like," Atherton said. "So I don't think there's an immediate threat there."

articles.title: 'Deserved justice': Why India boycotted presentation ceremony after Pakistan won Asia Cup - Explained
articles.summary: The Indian blind cricket team boycotted the presentation ceremony of the men's Asia Cup in Dhaka on Friday after Pakistan were declared champions even
articles.body: The Indian blind cricket team boycotted the presentation ceremony of the men's Asia Cup in Dhaka on Friday after Pakistan were declared champions even though the final was washed out without a ball being bowled. The decision led to a protest from the Cricket Association for the Blind in India (CABI), which said India and Pakistan should have been declared joint winners.Pakistan were awarded the title on the basis of a better net run rate. However, CABI general secretary Shailendra Yadav accused Pakistan of declaring themselves champions without following the position of the World Blind Cricket Council (WBCC) Technical Committee."I am deeply disappointed and strongly condemn the manner in which Pakistan has declared itself the winner of the Blind Cricket Asia Cup final without a single ball being bowled," Yadav said in a statement.Why did India protest Pakistan's title win?CABI argued that net run rate could not be used to decide the winner of a final that did not begin. According to Yadav, the criterion applied to the qualifying rounds and certain stages of a tournament, but could not automatically determine the outcome of a washed-out final."When rain prevents a single ball from being bowled in a final, the matter must be resolved strictly in accordance with the applicable tournament regulations and the decision of the WBCC Technical Committee."The possible outcomes should be determined through the prescribed provisions, whether that means a reserve day, a shared title or another officially authorised resolution," he said.CABI maintained that the two teams should have been declared joint winners because rain prevented any play in the final.What is CABI's allegation against the WBCC?CABI alleged that WBCC president and Pakistan Blind Cricket Council president Sultan Shah overruled the Technical Committee's decision to declare India and Pakistan joint winners.According to the association, the move forced the match referee to announce Pakistan as champions despite the committee's position.In a social media post, CABI said the decision had overshadowed the tournament's final and reiterated that India "deserved justice".The Indian team stayed away from the presentation ceremony in protest against the decision.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Focus on South Africans, Associates as ILT20 Season 5 prepares to get underway
articles.summary: Dubai: Faf du Plessis, David Miller, Tabraiz Shamsi, Heinrich Klaasen, Lizaad Williams and George Linde must have heaved a collective sigh of relief when
articles.body: Dubai: Faf du Plessis, David Miller, Tabraiz Shamsi, Heinrich Klaasen, Lizaad Williams and George Linde must have heaved a collective sigh of relief when the ILT20 calendar was announced. They might not have been the only ones. With the UAE-based T20 competition starting on November 21 this time -- avoiding an annual clash with South Africa's SA20 in the process -- the South Africans could play in both the competitions.Having played the first three seasons in January-February before moving to December-January last time around, the ILT20 has rescheduled the calendar even further this time. With the tournament now due to play its final on December 20, it will allow the likes of Du Plessis, Miller, Klaasen, Williams and Linde to make their debuts in the UAE.Not just the Proteas. Other players, such as Afghanistan's Rashid Khan, who would otherwise play portion of the ILT20 before jetting off to South Africa, can now play both in their entireties. SA20 Season 5 begins on January 17, 2027."My schedule opened up nicely to have this league open for me. It's always been a goal to come play in the UAE. I'm really looking forward to this competition. It's a strong competition. You just can't walk in here and think you're going to score runs and perform. You really need to be at your best. So that's also the biggest reason why I came to come play this league," said Gulf Giants captain Klaasen.Teammate and fellow South African Miller is equally pleased. "With the schedule for the year, with all the different leagues and international (cricket) and so on, I think it does become quite difficult to schedule these sort of tournaments. I am here, this time, because it's not overlapping with SA20. So I think it's a really good thing. It helps me to be here, so I'm really happy," added Miller.We as South Africans, we analyse the game quite well. We read the game quite well. So I think one of our strong qualities is we're good thinking brains.Over the last five years, the likes of Du Plessis, Quinton de Kock, Klaasen, Reeza Hendricks, Miller and Rilee Rossouw have set the T20 stage on fire, much like the players from the Caribbean did at one point.In tournaments involving more than five teams, Du Plessis has produced 5937 runs in this period; De Kock has blasted 5213 runs, Klaasen has 5066 runs and Hendricks is on 3386 runs. With 300 sixes, Klaasen has also brought the crowd to their feet. As have Du Plessis (273), Dewald Brevis (242) and Rossouw (239)."West Indian cricketers have been blessed with the genuine skills, the natural ability to go after the bowling and they displayed. That's why guys like Chris Gayle and all those guys started playing T20 around the world. So I think for us playing alongside these guys, you get to see what they do as well. We as South Africans, we analyse the game quite well. We read the game quite well. So I think one of our strong qualities is we're good thinking brains. That, with power of playing together and that's a good combination," explained Du Plessis on the eve of the competition.The focus, when Desert Vipers play the MI Emirates in the opener, will not just be on the Proteas. With each squad laden with at least four UAE players, four Afghanistan players, one Ireland player, one player each from Kuwait and Saudi Arabia, plus another from an ICC Associate Member country, it will be a massive learning curve for many.And that will not just be about occupying the dugout. Every playing XI must include at least two UAE players, two Afghanistan players and one Associate player. That last spot can even go to a third UAE player.And the UAE players were in demand at the auction. Muhammad Waseem commanded $210,000 from the MI Emirates. U-19 player Alishan Sharafu had Abu Dhabi Knight Riders shelling out $110,000. Aayan Khan and Muhammad Rohid pocketed $95,000 from Dubai Capitals and ADKR, respectively. USA's Amshi De Silva went to ADKR for $100,000."I think it's a great thing that the Associates has been included as a must-play member as well, because I honestly believe that there's a lot of Associate cricketers that are good enough to play in these leagues, but unfortunately, get overlooked. So it's nice to have Associate players.Sharjah Warriorz's Sikandar Raza finds it to be a useful rule that will allow the Associates to get some exposure and portray their talents."So I think it's going to be a very nice mixture of some unknowns mixed with the knowns. But for me, the most important thing would be who has the skillset to be going at one time looking at the data and matchups," he continued.QUICK SINGLESPlayers to watch🔴Defending champions Desert Vipers boast of Babar Azam, Naseem Shah, Fakhar Zaman, Shadab Khan and Shimron Hetmyer.🔴MI Emirates have Rashid Khan, Nicholas Pooran, Fazalhaq Farooqi and Romario Shepherd.🔴Heinrich Klaasen, David Miller and Liam Livingstone represent the Gulf Giants.🔴Dubai Capitals squad includes Faf du Plessis, Phil Salt, Marcus Stoinis and Mustafizur Rahman.🔴Finn Allen, Sunil Narine, Moeen Ali and Jason Holder will play for the Abu Dhabi Knight Riders.🔴Sharjah Warriorz have James Vince, Sikandar Raza, Mohammad Nabi and Adil Rashid in their midst.WILDCARDS🔴After the retentions and auction, teams were allowed to name their wildcards. And some heavyweights of T20 cricket will play the ILT20 Season 5.🔴ADKR have Andre Russell. Kieron Pollard will turn up for the MI Emirates for a fifth straight season. Tim Seifert is back with the Sharjah Warriorz. Sam Billings is in the Dubai Capitals camp. Akeal Hosein will be with the Gulf Giants while Tom Curran is at the Desert Vipers. NEW RULESBatter zone: ILT20 has introduced a "batter zone" at the popping crease. If the entire ball passes outside this designated area, it will be considered a wide, even if the batter has stepped across the stumps. The existing off-side wide lines and rules still apply to reverse sweeps and switch hits.Shot clock: Earlier, the shot clock applied only to the bowling team; now it will apply to the batting team as well. The batters must be ready for the next over within 60 seconds of the previous one ending. Two warnings will be given per innings. After that, each breach will cost five penalty runs. There are exemptions, however, for injuries, reviews, weather delays and strategic timeouts.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Josh Hazlewood hints at quitting if 'great leader' Pat Cummins loses captaincy as sandpapergate rocks Australia
articles.summary: Australia fast bowler Josh Hazlewood has said he would consider quitting the national team if Pat Cummins were removed as Test captain over allegations
articles.body: Australia fast bowler Josh Hazlewood has said he would consider quitting the national team if Pat Cummins were removed as Test captain over allegations that he knew about the ball-tampering scandal during the 2018 tour of South Africa.Hazlewood backed Cummins after Usman Khawaja, David Warner and, more recently, Cameron Bancroft claimed that “everyone knew” about the use of sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball. The 35-year-old supported Cummins' version of events that he was not involved in the plan.Hazlewood, who has taken 313 Test wickets, had signed a document in 2021 along with Cummins, Mitchell Starc and Nathan Lyon, denying any prior knowledge of sandpaper being “taken onto the field”.He described the criticism directed at Cummins since Bancroft published his 4,000-word column earlier this week as “a bit of a pile on” and backed the Australia captain's handling of the issue.“To get the group where it is now and in a position where something like that (sandpaper) is never going to happen again – I think is just a remarkable job,” Hazlewood told Code Sports, as quoted by Fox Sports.“He’s a great leader. If you went around and asked everyone in the team, you’d hear the same response."“I think if we turned up for the first Test and he wasn’t the captain and it was someone else, honestly, I don’t know how that would go.”Australia will face New Zealand in Perth in the first Test of the home summer, starting on December 9.Hazlewood also said he would consider not playing his 82nd Test if Cummins were forced to step down following Bancroft's claim that the Australia captain knew about the ball-tampering eight years ago.“I think I’d have to be put in that position to make a decision, but you’d have to think about it, yeah,” he said.Like Cummins, Hazlewood has publicly stood by his account of the events in 2018, saying he had “no knowledge” of ball-tampering during the South Africa series.“We were interviewed straight after (Cape Town) and I trust what I said in that two-three hour interrogation more than anything because it was in the day or two after,” Hazlewood said.“It was fresh in my mind at that point. Two things stand out for me from what’s been said. Was I an architect in the plan to tamper with the ball with sandpaper? And was I aware (of) sandpaper or foreign substances being used on the field?“The answer is no. When it boils down to it I think those two points are crucial.”The plan to use sandpaper, which was available in the dressing room for players to use on their bats, was first discussed during the tea break on the second day of the second Test at Port Elizabeth, when Australia were behind in the match.In his recent column, Bancroft alleged that then head coach Darren Lehmann and bowling coach David Saker were present when Warner first suggested using sandpaperGet the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND vs NZ 1st Test: Yashasvi Jaiswal, KL Rahul lead India's strong reply after New Zealand post 368
articles.summary: There has been constant chatter around Yashasvi Jaiswal’s exclusion from India’s ODI set-up and why he should feature in the 2027 World Cup side.
articles.body: There has been constant chatter around Yashasvi Jaiswal’s exclusion from India’s ODI set-up and why he should feature in the 2027 World Cup side. The young opener has the dual skill of defending and riding out difficult spells before seamlessly counter-attacking, a quality that can be invaluable in the Powerplay.India needed precisely those qualities at the Basin Reserve on Friday. After Henry Nicholls’s unbeaten 175 and Glenn Phillips’s 118 had carried New Zealand to 368 from 70 for five, Jaiswal’s sparkling 85 off 89 balls and KL Rahul’s unbeaten 52 off 116 powered India to 159 for one at stumps. The visitors remain 209 runs behind, but with nine wickets in hand and the pitch having eased considerably, the Test is set up beautifully.India had to go into survival mode early as Matt Henry and Kyle Jamieson bowled four successive probing maidens. It took India 26 balls to score their first run. Rahul was the beneficiary of some Kiwi largesse when New Zealand declined to review an LBW appeal off Henry. Replays indicated three reds. The hosts had already burnt a review on Rahul off Jamieson. It angered Henry, who tossed his jumper into the boundary hoardings when he saw the replay.Jaiswal was hardly secure himself. After an edged boundary, he was reprieved on six when Phillips failed to hold a sharp chance at gully off Jamieson. India went to tea at 16 for no loss after eight overs.On resumption, they cashed in. Jaiswal drove with authority and punished anything loose. He was also eager to bring some of his white-ball audacity into the Test arena, driving on the up, twice miscuing attempted slogs and ramping two fours over the slip cordon.He raced to his fifty and then ramped another boundary to bring up the century partnership. Barring South Africa, Jaiswal now has a 50-plus score in his first Test in the other three SENA countries.Rahul was the perfect foil, playing late, leaving judiciously and playing inside the line. He also put away anything directed at his pads. Their 130-run stand was India’s first century opening partnership in 17 Tests and their first in New Zealand since 1994.Jaiswal appeared set for a hundred before Henry finally won the battle. With wicketkeeper Tom Blundell standing up, Jaiswal nicked one behind. The appeal was turned down, but Henry screamed, “Big noise. Huge noise.” Latham reviewed this time and the spike on replay proved him right.Rahul, playing his first Test in New Zealand, then completed his fifty and became the only Indian opener with a 50-plus score in all SENA countries. He and Devdutt Padikkal ensured there was no late drama.Earlier, Phillips and Nicholls had threatened to bat India out of the contest. Resuming at 243 for five, the pair stretched their sixth-wicket partnership to 216. Phillips completed only his second Test hundred and became only the second batter after Rohit Sharma, against Sri Lanka in 2017, to score hundreds in all three formats against the same opposition in a calendar year.Nicholls, meanwhile, converted his hundred into a monumental unbeaten 175. India struggled for penetration with the second new ball before Akash Deep broke the partnership. Using the width of the crease, he created an angle against Phillips, and the ball held its line just enough to hit the stump, ending an outstanding knock of 118 off 216 balls.The last four wickets fell for just 30, restricting New Zealand to 368.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: IND vs NZ 1st Test: Akash Deep 2.0 is better, smarter and stronger
articles.summary: Even after receiving the generous acknowledgement of “well bowled” from Glenn Phillips, Akash Deep wasn’t quite ready to celebrate.
articles.body: Even after receiving the generous acknowledgement of “well bowled” from Glenn Phillips, Akash Deep wasn’t quite ready to celebrate. The New Zealand centurion had just been castled by a beauty, but the Dehri-born Bengal pacer first looked back at umpire Kumar Dharmasena to check whether his front foot had landed all right. Only after getting the nod from the Sri Lankan did Akash allow himself a celebration.Akash had good reason to look back and check. On his Test debut in Ranchi in Feb 2024, he had sent Zak Crawley’s off-stump cartwheeling, only for his joy to be cut short by the dreaded noball siren after umpire Rod Tucker got the message in his ear-piece from who else, but Dharmasena that Akash had overstepped. For someone who had waited so long for his India cap, after even having to fight with his late father for the right to pursue cricket instead of taking up a job, the wait for a maiden Test wicket was extended by a few more overs.His career since has followed a similarly stop-start path. One of the heroes of India’s 2-2 series draw in England, highlighted by his 10-wicket haul at Edgbaston in Aug 2025, Akash’s struggle-filled journey of economic hardship, grief and relentless hustle took another turn when he suffered a stress fracture of the back while playing the Ranji Trophy semifinal against Jammu & Kashmir in Kalyani last Feb.Just two months earlier, Kolkata Knight Riders had picked him up for Rs 1 crore after Lucknow Super Giants, who had paid Rs 8 cr for him, released him. Following surgery and months of rehabilitation at the Centre of Excellence in Bengaluru, Akash was grateful for the trust and support shown by the Indian team management.On Friday, returning to Test cricket after a 15-month hiatus, he repaid that faith with 3-53 from 23 overs. His previous Test appearance had come against England at the Oval.“GG sir (head coach Gautam Gambhir) used to follow up during that period and he would keep asking, ‘kaisa chal raha hain?’” Akash said after the day’s play. “During that time, I worked on my bowling and on areas I could improve. I wanted to get stronger. It didn’t feel like I was playing international cricket after nearly one and a half years.”Perhaps that was because Akash had already put plenty of miles into his legs. He bowled 23.2 overs in the Irani Cup against Rest of India in Srinagar, followed by 33 overs for Bengal against Delhi at Kalyani. He then delivered 35.3 overs in the first India A-New Zealand A game in Lincoln and another 23 in the second in Christchurch.Apart from rehabilitation at the COE, Akash used his time away to work on his craft. In 11 Tests, Akash has 31 wickets, with 11 of those victims bowled. Harry Brook, Joe Root, Zak Crawley, Ben Duckett and Ollie Pope feature on an impressive list of batters whose defences Akash has breached.Phillips, though, might rank as the best of the lot. Akash went wide on the crease and angled the ball in. After pitching, it moved away sharply to beat Phillips and rearrange his stumps. It was Bumrahesque, but Akash describes it matter-of-factly.“The ball wasn’t doing much, so I was trying to move wider of the crease to play with the mind of the batter. I was trying to make the batter play. So I went out. The batter started to play me, whereas he was leaving me earlier. Then I switched again, and got the wicket. I was trying to play with the batters’ mind,” Akash said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 'Making my job easier': CSK head coach Zaheer Khan breaks silence on MS Dhoni's 'unexpected' retirement
articles.summary: Chennai Super Kings head coach Zaheer Khan has admitted that MS Dhoni's decision to retire from playing in the Indian Premier League came as a surprise to
articles.body: Chennai Super Kings head coach Zaheer Khan has admitted that MS Dhoni's decision to retire from playing in the Indian Premier League came as a surprise to him, while describing the end of the former captain's playing career as an emotional moment for the franchise.Dhoni will no longer take the field for CSK but will remain associated with the five-time champions as their team mentor from IPL 2027. Zaheer said the team would miss having Dhoni as a player but was looking forward to working with him in his new role."It's been an emotional week for all of us, with mixed feelings. Every year, you're hoping that MS is going to be seen playing a role for the team this season. He will be, but in a different avatar, and hence the mixed feelings."I think the journey he has had in cricket has been amazing. Srinivasan rightly said that there is no CSK without MS, and that surely is the case," Zaheer said in a video uploaded on CSK's YouTube channel.Dhoni's retirement from playing was confirmed on November 17, when CSK announced that he would take up the role of team mentor.Zaheer said he was also looking forward to having Dhoni's experience and guidance as he takes charge of the team ahead of the next season."It's mixed feelings for me personally because you're not going to see him as part of the playing team. But I'm excited that he's going to be sharing the burden with me, making my job easier, guiding us in the right direction and being a mentor to us."So, yeah, excited about that, looking ahead, but also emotional about the decision he has taken," Zaheer added.Dhoni led CSK to five IPL titles and two Champions League T20 crowns. However, he did not play a single match during the 2026 season because of fitness concerns.While CSK owner Rupa Gurunath had earlier revealed that Dhoni had indicated he might not return as a player, Zaheer said he had not seriously considered the possibility. His focus, he explained, had been on preparing the squad and planning for the upcoming season."Not at all. I think, for a couple of reasons, it was the last year of this cycle. So maybe, looking ahead at a fresh cycle, those kind of thoughts would have popped into my head," Zaheer said."But right now, I wasn't even thinking about it. Obviously, you're looking at the season, you're looking at the stack-up of your team, the playing XI. I haven't personally given it a thought because, you know, it's MS. He knows what is the right thing to do and when is the time to act upon a certain thing."So I was not really spending my time and energy going in that direction. Whatever it is, it's going to be his decision. I'm planning for the season."So, yes, it was unexpected for me personally when he did mention it in a very, very subtle way, as you know, he doesn't like to create massive news out of it. It just was in the discussion, casually mentioning that, okay, this is it, you're going to have some extra money to go into the auction with," Zaheer added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: A perfect brew, a perfect blend: Rahul and Padikkal's coffee camaraderie
articles.summary: Wellington: The perfect blend for Devdutt Padikkal and KL Rahul isn't just at the crease.
articles.body: Wellington: The perfect blend for Devdutt Padikkal and KL Rahul isn't just at the crease. Off the field, the two batters share a growing obsession with coffee, one that began during India's 2024-25 tour of Australia and has now turned the dressing room into a brewing station of sorts. What started as a search for the perfect pour in Melbourne soon turned into an obsession with different roasts, beans, filters and brewing equipment."I think I deserve the credit for getting all of them, KL Rahul, Dhruv Jurel, into coffee. I think KL probably two or three years ago didn't even drink that much coffee. When we went to Australia, that's where we all really got into coffee. And it became an obsession for all of us."And once we came back, we just knew that we wanted that quality of coffee at home. So then it began. Then once you go down the rabbit hole of coffee, there are so many things to explore, so many different types of brewing methods and stuff like that. I'm really keen on coffee. And hopefully someday I would like to have a cafe in Bengaluru," Padikkal told TOI.The word spread, and players now carry their own equipment on home and away tours, no longer relying on instant sachets or powders at team hotels. Even during the ongoing series against New Zealand, Rahul, Padikkal, Jurel and Yashasvi Jaiswal, the latest to jump on the coffee bandwagon, are carrying their personal filters because there is no compromise. Before connecting bat to ball, that first cup of coffee is non-negotiable.If Padikkal has influenced Rahul's off-field choices, it is the other way around when the two batters are at the crease. Representing the same state in domestic cricket, they have played plenty of cricket together, and their understanding was evident as they blunted New Zealand on Day 2. Their 165-run stand frustrated the hosts, while their reading of the game was astute.The left-right pair were happy to negotiate maidens and didn't shy away from finding the release shot, even if it meant Rahul reverse-sweeping Glenn Phillips. They never lost control of the proceedings. New Zealand tried every trick in the book to disrupt their rhythm and concentration, but none worked. It didn't matter whether the wicketkeeper was standing up or back, whether the ball was old or new, or whether the field was attacking or defensive. The two were a picture of concentration.Only something supernatural could have dislodged them from their assured footing, and Kyle Jamieson found the magic in the 83rd over. It was déjà vu of sorts, as Akash Deep had done something similar to Glenn Phillips earlier in the Test. Padikkal could do little to counter that delivery. The left-hander lost his stumps just as he was within striking distance of a hundred and made sure to check the replay on the giant screen before walking off.After a job well done for the team, the coffee machine in the dressing room will be put to work. Dhruv Jurel is unlikely to be on barista duty, with the wicketkeeper-batter presumably padded up, but Jaiswal now has enough time on his hands to perfect the pour for his teammate. A fitting reward for a job well done.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Pat Cummins to remain Australia captain, given 'unanimous support' by cricket board amid Sandpapergate fallout
articles.summary: Pat Cummins confirms he will "100 per cent support" forum Cricket Australia has set up following Usman Khawaja's Sandpapergate allegations; CA chair David Boon rejects notion Cummins' integrity has been "compromised" amid varying accounts from players of 2018 ball-tampering scandal
articles.body:
Cummins' position had been under increasing scrutiny since Cameron Bancroft wrote a detail-filled account of the scandal in the West Australian newspaper , backing up Khawaja's claims that every member of the 2018 side was aware of the Sandpaper plot.

Bancroft - the player caught on camera trying to alter the condition of the ball in South Africa eight years ago - said he was stirred to break his silence by Cummins' vehement denials of knowledge of the scheme in a press conference last week.

After Cricket Australia chair David Boon and CEO Todd Greenberg met Cummins in Sydney on Friday, a statement released on Saturday read: "In the light of the ongoing speculation surrounding the Australian men's team tour of South Africa in 2018, the CA board met to ensure measures are in place to protect the integrity of Australian Cricket and the welfare of all concerned.

"As part of this meeting, the board resolved to express its unanimous support for Pat Cummins as captain given ongoing speculation about his position."

Cummins prepared for 'difficult conversations' in forum

Cummins, who is set to lead Australia in a four-Test series at home to New Zealand from December 9, with the first match in Bancroft's native Perth, said: "Being Australian captain carries with it an awesome responsibility.

"I have and never will take that lightly.

"David (Boon) and Todd (Greenberg) have a very tough job navigating cricket through all of this and I commend them for reaching out to me and to many of the players and staff from 2018.

"I support the forum 100 per cent. I will be there. All of the players and staff I have spoken with are very keen to have their say. There will be a lot of difficult conversations but that is what's needed.

"Otherwise, from this point, captaining the Australian team in Perth will be my focus and priority."

Boon: Cummins' integrity has not been compromised

Boon added: "We've expressed our support to Pat and our concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa.

"We have learned from that experience and are proud of the team and the culture Pat and other leaders in the team have fostered over the past eight years and unequivocally reject any implication that Pat's integrity has been compromised.

"We are absolutely determined to steward Australian cricket through this very difficult time with diligence and patience and to listen and learn.

"That's what the independent forum we announced this week is about and the board encourages all players and support staff to tell and discuss their stories there.

"We will be publishing the terms of reference in due course."

articles.title: IND vs NZ 1st Test: KL Rahul hits century, Shubman Gill misses ton by two runs as India dominate
articles.summary: KL Rahul led India's batting effort with a fine 136 as the visitors moved into a strong position in the first Test against New Zealand.
articles.body: KL Rahul led India's batting effort with a fine 136 as the visitors moved into a strong position in the first Test against New Zealand. India ended Day 3 at 486/4, taking a lead of 118 runs.Captain Shubman Gill came close to scoring a century but was dismissed for 98 in the final over of the day. Jacob Duffy bowled him just two runs short of the landmark. Rishabh Pant remained unbeaten on 55, while nightwatchman Anshul Kamboj was yet to open his account at stumps.Rahul and Padikkal put India in controlRahul once again showed his patience and skill in the longest format. He played a careful innings, defended well and scored runs whenever the bowlers gave him an opportunity. He faced 290 balls for his 136, hitting nine fours and two sixes. It was his 13th Test century.The knock also put Rahul in a special group. He became only the fourth Indian batter, after Sachin Tendulkar, Mohammad Azharuddin and Rahul Dravid, to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries — South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.Rahul found an able partner in Devdutt Padikkal. The two added 165 runs for the second wicket before Kyle Jamieson ended their partnership with a superb delivery that beat Padikkal's defence and hit the stumps. Padikkal made 80 off 175 balls. He was looking good for another Test hundred but fell short. It was his second half-century in Test cricket, having scored centuries in his previous two Test innings.Gill takes on the New Zealand attackAfter Padikkal's dismissal, Gill joined Rahul and kept the pressure on the New Zealand bowlers. Unlike Rahul, the Indian captain was more attacking and played several aggressive shots.The two added 91 runs for the third wicket. Gill took on Duffy, hitting him for a six with a pull shot to reach his half-century. He also attacked spinner Glenn Phillips, hitting him for a six over long-off.Rahul completed his century after lunch when he took a single. However, his stay at the crease ended when he tried to cut a delivery from Nathan Smith away from his body. The ball took the bottom of his glove before deflecting onto the stumps.Rahul walked back to a standing ovation from the Basin Reserve crowd after a fine innings.Pant and Gill add 100 runsAfter Rahul's dismissal, Pant joined Gill and the two continued India's attacking approach. They added 100 runs for the fourth wicket, putting the team in an even stronger position.Pant took time to settle down before shifting gears. He had scored only 15 runs from his first 37 balls but then smashed 37 runs off the next 18 deliveries.He hit Duffy for two sixes in a row and completed his 22nd half-century in Test cricket. Pant was unbeaten on 55 off 62 balls at the end of the day.Gill, meanwhile, was closing in on a century. But with only a few minutes left before stumps, Duffy produced a delivery that moved sharply back into him. Gill tried to push the ball forward, but it went past his bat, hit his pad and then crashed into the off stump.He walked back on 98, missing his century by just two runs.It was only the second time an Indian captain had been dismissed in the 90s against New Zealand in Test cricket. The first was MS Dhoni, who was also out for 98 against Daniel Vettori in Nagpur in 2010.Gill also moved to fourth place on the list of highest scores by an Indian captain in a Test in New Zealand. Azharuddin tops the list with 192 in Auckland in 1990, followed by Sunil Gavaskar's 116 in 1976 and Azharuddin's unbeaten 103 in Wellington in 1998.India score 327 runs on Day 3India made 327 runs and lost three wickets during the day's play. They began with a strong morning session, scoring 80 runs without losing a wicket.The second session brought 105 runs for the loss of one wicket, while India added another 142 runs and lost two wickets in the final session.India also increased their scoring rate as the day progressed. They scored an average of 2.96 runs per over in the first session, 3.88 in the second and 4.43 in the third. In simple terms, the batters scored more quickly as the day went on.New Zealand had made 368 in their first innings, with Henry Nicholls scoring an unbeaten 175. India now have a lead of 118 runs and will look to add more runs on Day 4 before putting New Zealand back in to bat.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's batting firepower came to the fore in the first Test against New Zealand in Wellington as the visitors scripted a piece of history, with all their top five batters scoring fifty-plus in the same innings in an away Test for the first time. A magnificent century from KL Rahul and valuable contributions from the rest of the top order put India firmly in the driver's seat, with a substantial 118-run lead at stumps on Day 3.After New Zealand posted a competitive 368 in their first innings, India responded with a commanding batting display, reaching a position of strength with two days remaining in the contest. The visitors' top five ensured there were no easy breakthroughs for the hosts, with every batter making a significant contribution to the first-innings total.The landmark achievement had previously occurred only four times in India's Test history, with all four instances coming on home soil. The Wellington Test against New Zealand in 2026 therefore became the first occasion when India's first five batters crossed the half-century mark in an overseas Test innings.India's top five create history in WellingtonThe historic effort was headlined by Rahul, who produced a patient and assured 136 off 290 deliveries, striking nine fours and two sixes. The opener's innings was particularly significant as he completed a century in all four SENA countries (South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia), underlining his credentials as one of India's most accomplished overseas batters.Yashasvi Jaiswal provided the perfect platform at the other end with an aggressive 85 off 89 balls, including 16 boundaries. Devdutt Padikkal continued the momentum with a composed 80 off 175 deliveries, striking 10 fours.Captain Shubman Gill came agonisingly close to another Test hundred, scoring 98 off 146 balls. His innings featured nine fours and two sixes before New Zealand pacer Jacob Duffy outsmarted him in the final over of the day.Rishabh Pant remained unbeaten on 55 off 62 balls, switching gears impressively after a cautious start. Having managed just 15 runs off his first 37 deliveries, the wicketkeeper-batter accelerated dramatically, scoring 37 off his next 18 balls to complete his half-century.India's top five to score fifty-plus in a Test inningsvs Australia, Kolkata, 1998vs New Zealand, Mohali, 1999vs Sri Lanka, Brabourne, 2009vs England, Dharamsala, 2024vs New Zealand, Wellington, 2026Rahul, Gill and Pant put India in commandIndia enjoyed a particularly productive third day, adding 142 runs in the final session despite losing two wickets. Rahul subsequently departed after making the mistake of playing away from his body, bringing an end to a knock that had put India in a commanding position.Gill and Pant then ensured New Zealand could not capitalise on those breakthroughs. articles.title: Sandpapergate: Former Australia head coach Darren Lehmann denies knowledge of sandpaper use after Cameron Bancroft allegations
articles.summary: Former Australia head coach Darren Lehmann has denied knowledge of the use of sandpaper, directly contradicting Cameron Bancroft's claims that the coaching staff were aware of the plot to tamper with the ball; Bancroft named Lehmann as present in the discussions around sandpaper use
articles.body:
The development comes after batter Cameron Bancroft - who was caught on camera using sandpaper - exacerbated the Sandpapergate scandal with a 4,000-word statement asserting that the entire team - including the bowling group - knew about the use of sandpaper on the three-Test tour of South Africa in 2018.

Bancroft named Lehmann as one of the members present in a discussion around the use of sandpaper, even quoting his former coach in directing an assistant to take the sandpaper from Bancroft once the ball-tampering had been discovered by the TV broadcast.

Lehmann has now denied those claims, telling BBC's Test Match Special: "No. I didn't know sandpaper was being used.

"I was coach at the time, I've got to take that responsibility.

"It was the best job in the world. I'm sorry for what happened."

The recollection of Lehmann, now Northamptonshire head coach, directly contradicts that of Bancroft, who was unequivocal in his belief that Lehmann was aware of the team's plot to tamper with the ball.

"Boof [Lehmann's nickname] shouted on the walkie talkie 'get the f***ing sandpaper off Bangers now'," Bancroft wrote in his statement on Wednesday.

"In my opinion, if he didn't know he wouldn't have said that. And if it wasn't clear enough before, then it was obvious now. Once again. WE ALL KNEW."

Lehmann denies knowledge of media manager's objections

Bancroft's lengthy statement detailed the discussions around the use of sandpaper that took place in the changing room, in which he claimed all players and coaches were present when media manager Kate Hutchinson made clear her opposition to the players' plan to alter the ball on day three of the second South Africa Test at Port Elizabeth.

Bowling coach David Saker resigned from the Australia set up in the wake of the scandal in 2019, before joining up with England's coaching team for the 2022 World Cup and 2023 Ashes.

Lehmann denied any knowledge of the meeting, saying: "No [I don't remember that].

"Everyone talks about meetings at the moment. There's a whole heap of meetings with different conversations going on - some people are privy to them and some people are not.

"I'm not privy to every conversation or meeting."

Lehmann was also quizzed directly on claims made in Khawaja's book which alleged that a member of the coaching staff told the team to use any means necessary to elicit reverse swing from the ball.

When asked whether that passage refereed to Lehmann or Saker, he responded: "I don't understand that statement as such.

"I didn't give that statement. I didn't get that question posed to me. I can't comment for anyone else."

When asked directly whether he was present for a conversation where then vice-captain David Warner raised the possibility of sandpaper use, Lehmann responded: "I can't remember being present during that conversation.

"It was eight and a half years ago. You'll have to ask those people.

"That's the issue - I have my version and that's where I stand."

The former head coach did concede that punishments for the ball-tampering plot - which saw Warner and Steve Smith stripped of their leadership positions and banned for a year, alongside Bancroft's nine-month ban - could have been distributed more evenly.

When asked whether the blame attributed to the three players punished was fair, Lehmann responded: "Probably not.

"It's so long ago, and that was the decision that was made - we just have to respect that.

"It's not ideal for anyone. For me, the punishment didn't fit the crime - but it was a bad time, and I take responsibility for that."

Backing for Cummins, Hazlewood criticises 'pile on'

Lehmann's claims add to a furore of discussion around the 2018 scandal since the publication of Khawaja's book first brought to light claims the entire team knew about the use of sandpaper.

Khawaja also alleged discussions about ball-tampering had been held "openly and lightheartedly" across the entire squad, involving not just the batters, bowlers and coaching staff but the wider team.

Those claims align with Bancroft's, and with the recollection of former seamer Chadd Sayers , who also asserted that "everyone in that [2018] side" was aware of the ball-tampering taking place on the tour.

Cummins, who earlier on Saturday received "unanimous support" from Cricket Australia to continue as Test and ODI captain, called Khawaja's claims "complete and utter nonsense" during a sensational 68-minute press conference on Friday of last week.

He was also backed up by fellow fast bowler Josh Hazlewood, who criticised the "pile on" against Cummins, saying he would consider his position in the Test side if he was forced to stand down as captain.

Hazlewood's comments followed those of another bowler in Mitchell Starc, who earlier this month also claimed "his recollection hadn't changed since 2021" when the bowlers released a joint statement denying knowledge.

Bancroft's detailed claims also came in the wake of Cricket Australia announcing an independent forum to explore the scandal. It stated players could share their version of events without fears of reprisals.

articles.title: Sandpapergate: Pat Cummins' integrity not compromised - Cricket Australia
articles.summary: Cricket Australia has "unequivocally rejected" the suggestion that captain Pat Cummins' integrity has been compromised by the sandpaper scandal.
articles.body:
Cricket Australia has "unequivocally rejected" the suggestion that captain Pat Cummins' integrity has been compromised by the sandpaper scandal.

On Saturday CA gave its "unanimous support" to Cummins, and he said he would take part in the independent forum set up for players and staff.

Cummins has faced claims to step down as captain after Cameron Bancroft's detailed testimony supported claims made by Usman Khawaja that the entire Australia team knew of the plan to tamper with the ball during a Test against South Africa in Cape Town in 2018.

CA and Cummins met this week, with the former saying it was "determined to steward Australian cricket through this very difficult time with diligence and patience and to listen and learn".

"We've expressed our support to Pat and our concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa," CA said.

"We have learned from that experience and are proud of the team and the culture Pat and other leaders in the team have fostered over the past eight years and unequivocally reject any implication that Pat's integrity has been compromised."

CA chief executive Todd Greenberg said Cummins has been an "exemplary leader" in his five years as captain.

"He has consistently spoken and articulated what happened back in 2018 in his version of events. Nothing's changed. Thus, nothing's changing with our captaincy," Greenberg told BBC Sport.

Greenberg acknowledged that people's version of events "directly contradict" each other but said Cummins has "not moved one inch" from his story, giving the same account now as he did when interviewed the day after the Cape Town Test in 2018.

Cummins is due to lead Australia in the opening match of a four-Test series against New Zealand starting on 9 December in Perth.

The pace bowler reiterated his stance that he had no involvement in or knowledge of the sandpaper plot during a 68-minute news conference last week.

Cummins has said he will attend the forum that has been set up by CA for players and staff to share their version of events.

"I support the forum 100%. I will be there," he said.

"All of the players and staff I have spoken with are very keen to go and to have their say.

"There will be a lot of difficult conversations, but that is what's needed.

"Otherwise, from this point, captaining the Australian team in Perth will be my focus and priority."

The row over the sandpaper saga, one of the biggest controversies in Test history, has engulfed Australian sport since Khawaja's claims emerged two weeks ago.

In 2018 Bancroft was banned for nine months and captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner for a year after Bancroft was caught rubbing sandpaper on the ball during the third Test at Newlands.

Khawaja, who retired from international cricket this year, wrote in his autobiography that all the Australia team knew and should have taken responsibility. He has since been supported by Warner and bowlers Chadd Sayers and Jon Holland.

Cummins' said in his news conference that Khawaja's assertions were "100% wrong" and "nonsense".

Fox Sports has taken Khawaja and Warner off commentary duties for the next few weeks.

Fox Sports managing director Steve Crawley said it was "unfair" to put them in a position where it would be "difficult to focus on the game".

In backing Cummins, Greenberg said he was not accusing Bancroft, Khawaja and Warner of lying.

"I'm not putting someone's version of events over somebody else's," he said.

"I don't think they're lying, but I can't tell you what they know and what they don't know. I can only take on face value what they're saying."

Greenberg said it was an "almost impossible" task to put together the truth of what happened given people have different recollections of what happened.

He said CA is "determined" to give everyone the opportunity to have their say "without judgement" in the forum and share as much information as possible to "put a full stop on this once and for good".

articles.title: Pakistan drop Mohammad Rizwan, Shan Masood and Imam-ul-Haq as PCB finally announces long-delayed central contracts
articles.summary: Pakistan have announced their much-delayed central contracts for 38 players, with former captains Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood, along with opener
articles.body: Pakistan have announced their much-delayed central contracts for 38 players, with former captains Mohammad Rizwan and Shan Masood, along with opener Imam-ul-Haq, among the notable omissions from the new list released by the Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) on Saturday.The announcement comes after a considerable delay, with the previous central contracts having expired on June 30. The PCB has introduced a new format-based structure, dividing players into separate Test, ODI and T20 categories, alongside a development category that accommodates the majority of the contracted players.The exclusions of Rizwan, Shan and Imam come amid recent setbacks in their international careers. Shan was recently removed as Pakistan's Test captain, while Rizwan and Imam were sent back home from England during Pakistan's tour, following which the visitors suffered a 3-0 whitewash in the Test series.Former captain Shadab Khan has also seen his status reduced, receiving a contract only in the T20 category.Babar, Salman the only players in Test and ODI categoryTest captain Babar Azam and Salman Ali Agha are the only two players included in the combined Test and ODI category. ODI captain Shaheen Shah Afridi has been placed in the ODI/T20 category, while Sahibzada Farhan, who led Pakistan in their most recent T20 Internationals, has received a contract exclusively in the T20 category.Among the other notable omissions are all-rounder Aamer Jamal, Saim Ayub, young pacer Akif Javed and spinner Ali Usman. articles.title: How Joe Root, Harry Brook videos helped KL Rahul prepare for New Zealand challenge
articles.summary: KL Rahul prepared for his first Test assignment in New Zealand by studying how England batters Joe Root and Harry Brook handled the conditions.
articles.body: KL Rahul prepared for his first Test assignment in New Zealand by studying how England batters Joe Root and Harry Brook handled the conditions. Watching their videos helped him believe that scoring runs in New Zealand was not an impossible task.The preparation paid off as Rahul scored 136 off 290 balls in the first Test in Wellington. His 13th Test century took India to 486/4 on Day 3 and gave them a lead of 118 runs.The knock also helped Rahul complete a special achievement. He became only the fourth Indian batter, after Sachin Tendulkar, Mohammad Azharuddin and Rahul Dravid, to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries — South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.“Watched a lot of videos of Joe Root and Harry Brook while preparing. That gave me confidence that it’s not impossible to score here,” Rahul said after the third day's play.Rahul changes his approachRahul believes his batting technique was never the reason behind his difficult phase. He said the bigger challenge was to change his approach and understand when to leave the ball rather than trying to play every delivery.During his 15 months in the middle order, Rahul had developed a habit of putting his bat to almost every ball. He realised that this could be risky in conditions where the ball moves after pitching."Technique was never an issue," Rahul said during the post-day press conference. He explained that he had worked on finding the right guard and batting position to give himself the best chance in New Zealand."During those 15 months in the middle order, I developed a habit of putting bat on ball. In seaming conditions, having less contact between bat and ball could be the best approach."Rahul also spoke about how he used his practice sessions to understand the conditions and prepare for the challenge."I wasn't looking at anything specific when I entered the nets. I just played a lot of balls to figure out what guard and positions I needed to adopt to give myself the best chance. There are no guarantees, though. I watched videos of guys who had scored runs in New Zealand earlier," he said.India A struggles did not stop himRahul did not score many runs during the India A matches before the Test series. However, he did not let those performances affect his preparation. Instead, he spent more time in the nets and worked on his game."It feels awesome to achieve something like that. I have been here for a good three weeks and didn't get a lot of runs for India A, but spent a lot of time in the nets to understand how to score runs. I had clear plans," he said."When you work hard, it translates into performance," he added.Speaking about completing his collection of Test hundreds in all four SENA countries, Rahul said:“Feels awesome to achieve something like that,” he said.He also described his approach at the start of the third day's play.“Didn’t get runs in India A games but used the nets to get myself ready. Had very clear plans on how I wanted to play. Getting results in first innings always helps, and I am very happy”“Didnt go with any plan in morning. I knew what the wicket was doing, was importsnt to start well and start tight. Continued to keep batting and there was no message or anything.“I dont think I was fired up, I don’t think I ever get fired up.”'I never get fired up'The Wellington Test was Rahul's first appearance in New Zealand in his 71-match Test career. Despite the opportunity to achieve a special milestone, he said he was not particularly fired up.For him, the match was about testing himself against a strong bowling attack."I never get fired up. This was an opportunity I didn't want to lose. When you play Tests for that long, you get that opportunity to challenge yourself against the best attack," he said.Rahul also shared his thoughts on the Basin Reserve pitch. He felt the surface was starting to help the spinners, with some deliveries keeping low and rough patches beginning to develop."The ball will keep low and some rough patches are developing, which could get bigger as we bowl more. We will hope the track deteriorates, but not until we are batting," he said.Rahul praises India's bowlers and JaiswalRahul felt the toss and India's disciplined bowling in the first session had helped keep New Zealand's first-innings score under control.New Zealand made 368 runs, with Henry Nicholls scoring an unbeaten 175."When we first got here, we didn't think it would play like this. We had seen some scores and expected it to do a little more. The toss was important."Our bowlers did well in the first session and ensured that they didn't score 550 or 600 runs. We would take 368, as it gave us enough time to score the runs," he said.Rahul also had words of praise for opening partner Yashasvi Jaiswal. The two added 130 runs for the first wicket, giving India their first century opening partnership in New Zealand in 32 years.The last time India had a century opening stand in the country was in 1994, when Navjot Sidhu and Nayan Mongia put together 102 runs.Rahul said Jaiswal's attacking style was the result of hard work and regular training."Jaiswal is a very hard-working cricketer. He trains very hard to be the ultra-aggressive batter that he has become. It doesn't happen by chance," he said."We get along well off the field, and that reflects in our on-field performance," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sandpapergate fallout: Usman Khawaja, David Warner pulled from commentary duties amid fresh storm
articles.summary: The fallout from Australia's explosive Sandpapergate controversy has taken another turn, with broadcaster Fox Cricket taking former openers Usman Khawaja
articles.body: The fallout from Australia's explosive Sandpapergate controversy has taken another turn, with broadcaster Fox Cricket taking former openers Usman Khawaja and David Warner off its commentary roster as fresh revelations about the 2018 ball-tampering scandal continue to rock Australian cricket.Fox Sports managing director Steve Crawley confirmed that both commentators would be rested from broadcasts over the next few weeks, acknowledging that the continuing controversy had made it increasingly difficult for them to concentrate on their broadcasting responsibilities. No return date has been announced.“In light of recent events, both Usman and Davey will be rested from our broadcasts over the next few weeks,’’ Crawley told CODE Sports.“While we always support all members of our commentary team and welcome a diversity of views, which is a feature of our summer of cricket, we also understand the pressure they are under to respond to every new comment," he added.“We think it is increasingly difficult to focus on the game while the situation continues to unfold and think it is unfair on both commentators to put them in that position," he said.“Our focus remains on providing our viewers with the best broadcast of Australia’s summer of cricket. We will continue to monitor the situation," he concluded.Khawaja, Bancroft revelations reignite SandpapergateThe controversy has resurfaced following revelations in Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr, and subsequent comments from Cameron Bancroft suggesting that knowledge of the ball-tampering plan extended beyond the three players who were initially sanctioned.Bancroft was caught using sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball during the Cape Town Test against South Africa in March 2018. The scandal resulted in suspensions for then captain Steve Smith, vice-captain Warner and Bancroft, triggering one of the biggest crises in Australian cricket.In his autobiography, Khawaja questioned the extent of knowledge within the Australian dressing room about the plan. Bancroft subsequently added fuel to the controversy through a column in The West Australian, alleging that the wider squad was aware of what was happening and that discussions about generating reverse swing had involved members of the bowling group, including Pat Cummins.Bancroft described Cummins' recent press conference as the 'final straw' that prompted him to break his silence.Cummins rejects allegations as CA backs captainCummins strongly rejected the allegations when questioned about them in Sydney, describing the suggestion that the entire team knew about the plan as "complete and utter nonsense".The renewed controversy has put Australia's Test captain under scrutiny, with questions emerging over his position amid the fresh claims. Cricket Australia, however, has backed Cummins to continue as skipper, issuing a statement of support.Australia face England in the first of five T20 Internationals at the Melbourne Cricket Ground on Saturday, before opening their home Test summer against New Zealand at Perth Stadium on December 9.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates.
