articles.title: Another fifty, another statement! Devdutt Padikkal strengthens No.3 claim: 'Always great to get some runs'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India's search for a dependable number three in Test cricket could finally be yielding results, with Devdutt Padikkal strengthening his case
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India's search for a dependable number three in Test cricket could finally be yielding results, with Devdutt Padikkal strengthening his case for the crucial position through another composed half-century against New Zealand in the first Test in Wellington.The left-hander scored a patient 80 off 175 deliveries, helping India take control of the contest after New Zealand posted 368 in their first innings. Padikkal shared a crucial 165-run partnership with KL Rahul (136), ensuring India did not allow the hosts to claw their way back into the match on the third day.India reached 486/4 at stumps, establishing a 118-run lead with two days remaining. For Padikkal, it was another significant contribution in a promising start to his Test career, having now registered four scores of fifty or more in seven innings across five matches."It's always great to get some runs," Padikkal said after the day's play. "It was important that me and KL (Rahul) started off the day well. It was important that we didn't let them back into the game, and I think we did that pretty well today."Rahul partnership key to keeping New Zealand at bayResuming at 159/1 on Day 3, Rahul and Padikkal ensured India negotiated the morning session without losing a wicket. The Karnataka batter said surviving that crucial period was central to their partnership and India's subsequent dominance."Yeah, like I said, it was important that we got through that first session. I think if they were able to pick up a couple of wickets early, it would have put us in a bit of a difficult position," he explained."But I think that was the conversation, just building that partnership and taking it as deep as possible. And once we were able to do that, then it was our turn to put pressure back on them. And I think we did that well."Padikkal reached his half-century off 98 balls before continuing to build on the partnership. His innings eventually ended when Kyle Jamieson produced a delivery that straightened and clipped the top of off stump.The 26-year-old also spoke about his first experience of playing in New Zealand, admitting that the conditions at the Basin Reserve were different from what the Indian batters had anticipated."Yeah, it's a great ground. It's my first time in New Zealand. I really enjoyed being out here and this was a great venue to play cricket at. And hopefully we can continue to play some good cricket and get a win with us," he said.Padikkal focused on extending India's leadPadikkal revealed that India had expected more assistance for the seamers from the surface but had found the pitch considerably flatter than anticipated."Yeah, definitely. I think we expected a lot, a lot of grass on the wicket. We expected a lot of movement. It's probably not panned out that way. It's been much flatter than we expected. But at the same time, it's important that you respect the conditions that are in front of you."He added: "I think it was important that we continue to score big. And that's the conversation in the dressing room as well. Everyone's really confident. Everyone's had a lot of preparation behind them coming into this Test match and that shows."Padikkal, who made his Test debut in 2024, established himself as a contender for the number three position when India gave him the opportunity during the Sri Lanka series earlier this year.In five Tests and seven innings, he has accumulated 498 runs at an impressive average of 71.14, including two centuries and two half-centuries. His latest contribution in Wellington further strengthens his credentials as India look to settle their top order.With India already holding a substantial lead, Padikkal stressed that the focus was on building an even bigger advantage rather than looking too far ahead."Not yet. We are not looking too far ahead. It's important that we take one session at a time. I think definitely we are in a really good position right now. But it's important that we really extend that lead as much as possible so that we can put more pressure on them."India will resume Day 4 with six wickets in hand, looking to build on their advantage and put New Zealand under further pressure.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 'He's not the only one': NZ bowling coach backs Jacob Duffy after expensive outing against India
articles.summary: New Zealand bowling coach Jacob Oram has thrown his weight behind Jacob Duffy after the fast bowler endured a difficult outing on day three of the first
articles.body: New Zealand bowling coach Jacob Oram has thrown his weight behind Jacob Duffy after the fast bowler endured a difficult outing on day three of the first Test against India at the Basin Reserve in Wellington. Duffy conceded 181 runs in his spell, including seven no-balls, as India took control of the contest with a commanding batting display.Despite the expensive figures, Oram insisted that one difficult day should not overshadow Duffy's recent performances and consistent hard work. The New Zealand coach also pointed to the pacer's achievements over the last two seasons, saying he has earned enough credit to move past a disappointing performance.Oram highlights Duffy's hard work and commitmentOram said the 30-year-old pacer should not be judged on the basis of one expensive performance, especially after the consistency he has shown over the past two seasons."Jacob Duffy is fine. I mean, you should know, we try not to get too high when things are good and we try not to get too low when things haven't gone your way. So today, if you just look at the scoreboard, it's not his day."But he's had way too many good days in the last two seasons for one day to suddenly put him in the depths of despair. So he'll be okay. At the same time, he knows he's got areas to work on and improve, but he's not the only one in the dressing room," Oram said during the post-day press conference.Duffy continues to work on his game despite successOram also pointed out that Duffy's commitment to improving his bowling has remained consistent, even during the most successful phases of his career.According to Oram, Duffy continued working on different aspects of his bowling even while collecting individual honours and enjoying opportunities at the highest level."I don't want to go into specifics, to be honest, just because the dude went for a few runs. But I say again, guys are always working on stuff. Even before this Test, he was working on stuff. Even last season, when he won the Sir Richard Hadlee Medal and the Players' Cap, he was working on things."I know right now I'm sitting here and you can say it's lip service because he's had a bad day, but the guy is always working hard. I think when you see where he's got to with those awards, with the IPL opportunity he got and with some other stuff coming his way, that's how these guys stay where they are because he's always working on stuff – his run-up, delivery stride and wrist position. But even if he's bowling well, we're still working on things," he added.Day 3 report: Rahul, Gill and Padikkal put India in controlMeanwhile, India produced a dominant batting performance on the third day of the opening Test to take a commanding 118-run first-innings lead against New Zealand.Resuming their innings at 159/1, India finished the day at 486/4 in 125 overs, with KL Rahul leading the charge through a magnificent 136 off 290 deliveries. The opener struck nine boundaries and two sixes to register his 13th Test century.Devdutt Padikkal provided excellent support with an impressive 80 off 175 balls, sharing a crucial 165-run partnership with Rahul for the second wicket. Kyle Jamieson eventually broke the stand by dismissing Padikkal.Rahul later combined with captain Shubman Gill for another important partnership before Nathan Smith ended his innings.Gill continued India's dominance with an aggressive 98 off 146 deliveries, striking nine fours and two sixes. However, he fell agonisingly short of his 12th Test century after Duffy bowled him in the final over of the day.Rishabh Pant also made a significant contribution, remaining unbeaten on 55 off 62 balls. He shared a 100-run partnership with Gill to further strengthen India's position.New Zealand, who had posted 368 in their first innings, struggled to contain the Indian batters on a pitch that increasingly favoured batting. Jamieson and Smith picked up one wicket each, while Duffy finished with one wicket for 180 runs according to the day's scorecard.Brief scores: New Zealand 368 all out; India 486/4 (KL Rahul 136, Shubman Gill 98, Devdutt Padikkal 80, Rishabh Pant 55*). articles.title: Shubman Gill, Rishabh Pant script history, become first two Indians to achieve major WTC milestone
articles.summary: Shubman Gill and Rishabh Pant etched their names in the record books during India's first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington,
articles.body: Shubman Gill and Rishabh Pant etched their names in the record books during India's first Test against New Zealand at the Basin Reserve in Wellington, becoming the first two Indian batters to cross the 3,000-run mark in the ICC World Test Championship (WTC).Gill was the first to reach the landmark on Saturday, achieving the feat during a commanding innings of 98 on Day 3 of the opening Test. Pant followed him later in the day, becoming the second Indian to enter the exclusive club. He also created history by becoming the first wicketkeeper in the world to score 3,000 runs in the WTC.Having accumulated 2,917 runs in 76 innings before the Wellington Test, Gill needed 83 more to reach the milestone. The India captain got there in style, clearing the boundary off Glenn Phillips for a six in the 115th over during the third session. He went on to make 98 before Jacob Duffy bowled him on the third-last delivery of the day's play, leaving him just two runs short of a century.Pant, meanwhile, had 2,948 WTC runs heading into the contest and required another 52 to reach the 3,000-run mark. The wicketkeeper-batter completed the milestone with a boundary in the 123rd over, an effort that also brought up his 22nd Test half-century. He remained unbeaten on 55 off 62 deliveries at stumps.Interestingly, Gill's achievement also continued a sequence of Indian batters reaching successive WTC run milestones. Ajinkya Rahane was the first Indian to register 1,000 runs in the championship, followed by Rohit Sharma, who became the first to reach 2,000. Gill has now become the first Indian to breach the 3,000-run barrier.India's batting dominance on Day 3The milestones came during a prolific batting effort from India, who finished Day 3 at 486/4, establishing a lead of 118 runs over New Zealand's first-innings total of 368.KL Rahul headlined the effort with a magnificent 136, becoming the first Indian opener to score Test centuries in all four SENA countries - South Africa, England, New Zealand and Australia.Yashasvi Jaiswal had laid the foundation with an 85 on Day 2, while Devdutt Padikkal chipped in with 80. It was also the first time India's top five batters had all registered scores of at least 50 in the same Test innings outside India.With Pant unbeaten alongside nightwatchman Anshul Kamboj, who was on nought after negotiating the final two deliveries, India ended the day firmly in control of the contest.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Australia beat England in first T20I as MCG record run-chase earns hosts 1-0 lead in five-match series
articles.summary: Harry Brook hits 68 off 25 balls after being dropped twice, as Australia put down six chances in the field; England add only 68 from final 10 overs, as hosts chase 188 with a ball to spare; second T20I takes place in Carrara on Tuesday (play starts 8.15am UK time)
articles.body:
England captain Harry Brook had tonked 68 off just 25 balls - hitting six sixes - as England posted 187-9, though his side wasted a dominant position of 119-4 at the halfway point of their innings by adding only 68 from the last 10 overs.

Nikhil Chaudhary, who had helped drag Australia back into the contest with the ball - the hosts having dropped six chances - then top-scored with a magnificent 68 off 38 with the bat.

He was dismissed with 20 still required off the final two overs, Australia seven down, but Jack Edwards (25no off 11) struck a couple of crucial sixes in a clutch cameo before finishing the job with a boundary.

After being inserted by the hosts, England's innings had got off to the worst possible start as Phil Salt picked out mid-off first ball, while Aneurin Donald (10) - put down two deliveries prior - perished soon after.

But Brook, dropped on 2 and 3, made Australia pay for their profligacy as he smoked three sixes in a row in taking Riley Meredith's fourth over for 24, the touring captain romping to a 20-ball fifty.

He and Tom Banton (39 off 22) - shelled twice, taking Australia's tally to five inside seven overs - put on 107 for the third wicket, with Adam Zampa also taking some tap as his opening over went for 20.

Both were gone in the space of six deliveries though, Chaudhary's wrist spin accounting for Brook, caught behind, and Banton gone to a sensational diving catch in the deep by debutant Lachlan Shaw.

England stumbled their way to a rather underwhelming score thereafter, despite the best efforts of Jordan Cox (27 off 20) and Sam Curran (21 off 20), the visitors falling short of the 200-run target they'll have surely been eyeing.

That said, it was still a record T20I chase at the MCG for Australia to reel in, and their assignment was made all the tougher when Liam Dawson (1-30) struck in the opening over - Jake Fraser-McGurk (1) bowled when charging the left-arm spinner, deceived in the flight.

Mitch Marsh hammered Henry Crocombe's first ball in T20 international cricket for six over deep backward square for quite the introduction, but the young quick responded well to remove fellow debutant Sam Harper (32 off 15) for his first wicket in his second over.

Harper had provided some impetus to the Australian innings, Jamie Overton's opening over plundered for 21 runs, and Chaudhary maintained that momentum, with useful support from his captain Marsh (37 off 32) and Tim David (20 off 13).

David failed to cash in a huge slice of luck when the bails failed to dislodge as he inside-edged one back onto his stumps, as he departed a ball later to the returning Adil Rashid (1-30).

It prompted a rather sizeable Australian wobble, with three wickets tumbling for 13 runs in little more than an over, and when Chaudhary finally fell - caught in the deep - it looked like England might be in the ascendency, only for Edwards to have other ideas.

In other worrying news for England, Will Jacks left the field late on, splitting the webbing on his hand as Ben Dwarshuis drilled a ball back at him in the penultimate over. He is due to captain the team in the fifth and final T20I of the series as Brook departs for the Test tour of South Africa.

articles.title: Shubman Gill and the art of spotting his father in the stands
articles.summary: WELLINGTON: When Shubman Gill reached his half-century with an authoritative pull, the Indian captain raised his bat towards the stands behind square leg.
articles.body: WELLINGTON: When Shubman Gill reached his half-century with an authoritative pull, the Indian captain raised his bat towards the stands behind square leg. He has a knack for spotting his father, Lakhwinder Gill, dressed in his “lucky” white kurta-pyjama, no matter how crowded the stands are. Gill Sr. can make the task a little challenging with his habit of changing positions, but on Saturday, he knew exactly where his family would be seated.When India resumed batting on Day 2, Lakhwinder was seated right behind the bowler's arm. But as the wind picked up, he moved in search of some warmth from the sunshine and joined his wife, Keart Gill, on the benches near the museum. By the time Gill walked out to bat, the Indian captain would have known that his father's position was now fixed. The sunshine was just what Lakhwinder needed as the temperature dipped.It was an innings of complete control from the captain, who missed out on a deserved hundred by just two runs but ensured India were firmly in a position of dominance. He added 91 runs with KL Rahul before stitching together a breezy 100-run partnership with Rishabh Pant, maintaining the tempo throughout. Gill brought up his half-century off just 66 deliveries and kept India's momentum going even after the dismissals of Devdutt Padikkal and Rahul.There was a sense of urgency, but Gill never allowed desperation to creep into his 146-ball knock. He kept bisecting the field with precision and wasn't afraid to go aerial whenever the pressure began to build. New Zealand tried a double trap, stationing two catchers on the off side to capitalise on mistimed drives while packing the field for the pull and hook shots. Gill wasn't perturbed. He made room to dispatch the short deliveries through the covers and was particularly strong through the leg side.By then, New Zealand had realised that Gill wasn't falling for any bait and would have hoped for a lapse in concentration to breach his defence. A moment of uncertainty arrived with a close LBW appeal, but replays suggested an inside edge, prompting the umpire's call to be overturned. Rishabh Pant urged him to review the decision. Just when the cameras were ready to capture a second raise of the bat, possibly followed by another acknowledgement towards the same section of the stands, an anti-climax awaited.Gill fell for 98. It would have been his first Test hundred on New Zealand soil. A Jacob Duffy delivery, angling in, breached his defences, and a frustrated Gill began the long walk back to the dressing room.His father, Lakhwinder, shared the disappointment. But he will be back in the stands in Christchurch, wearing the same white kurta-pyjama, hoping his son spots him once again.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Lot of videos, hours in the nets and a solid game plan: How KL Rahul cracked the New Zealand code
articles.summary: Wellington: \"Feels really awesome, actually, to be able to achieve something like that,\" said KL Rahul, visibly pleased after achieving the rare feat of
articles.body: Wellington: "Feels really awesome, actually, to be able to achieve something like that," said KL Rahul, visibly pleased after achieving the rare feat of scoring Test centuries in all four SENA countries as an opener. He reached the milestone on Day 3 of the first Test against New Zealand and was delighted to make a substantial contribution in India's first innings.Rahul arrived in New Zealand early to begin his preparations, following his usual routine, and also squeezed in an India A game before the Tests. His returns weren't particularly encouraging, and the subsequent ODI series didn't give him much time at the crease. However, Rahul made the most of his net sessions in Christchurch, Auckland and Wellington."I didn't get a lot of runs in that India A game. But I used the time in the nets and tried to figure out how I could give myself the best chance to succeed in these conditions. There's a lot of Test cricket under me, a lot of experiences, good and bad. I just had very clear plans before I came here as to how I wanted to play. And I'm happy that I could go out there and do that and get the results in the first innings. That's performances and runs," Rahul said at the end of the day's play.New Zealand is now the fifth country in which Rahul has reached the three-figure mark, and this century will arguably taste the sweetest. Twelve years after making his Test debut, this was his first outing in this part of the world, and he certainly left his mark. Rahul arrived with a plan, stuck to it and never deviated from the methods that have brought him immense success in the ongoing World Test Championship (WTC) cycle.Rahul enjoyed considerable success in England last year, looked solid in Sri Lanka and has now carried that consistency into New Zealand. The build-up to the tour revolved around the challenges of batting in these conditions. When the teams arrived at the Basin Reserve, the talk surrounding the 15mm grass cover took centre stage. Add to that the possibility of strong winds and persistent cloud cover.All the chatter, however, did little to distract Rahul, who had done extensive homework by watching videos of recent Test matches. His research convinced him that scoring runs here was very much possible, while the examples of Joe Root and Harry Brook gave him the confidence he needed."I've been thinking about Test cricket in New Zealand for the last six or seven months, trying to do my homework, trying to see the guys who have scored runs here and how they've been able to achieve that. And once I got the opportunity, if I ticked all those boxes, then it becomes slightly easier when you play the game."I watched the last few years of Test cricket here. England played here, Australia played here, West Indies were here recently. So, yeah, I just pulled out some videos and asked the analysts to send me footage of guys who've scored runs here. Joe Root was there, Harry Brook scored a lot of runs. I just watched how they went about it. It gave me a little confidence that it's not impossible to score runs in New Zealand. It requires a very clear game plan," Rahul explained.There were passages of play when Rahul became the cushion absorbing all the pressure, but he never looked out of place. He weathered the storm, allowed his partners to take charge whenever required and remained steadfast at the other end. He was at peace with his methods and had remarkable clarity of mind. There were a few nervy moments after he walked out to bat, including a close LBW appeal and some inside edges, but Rahul dug deep to bring up his 10th overseas hundred. Interestingly, only three of his 13 Test centuries have come at home."I will buy Glenn Phillips a few drinks after the game for not reviewing that. Those were the slowest 15 seconds of my life. Kept hoping people would listen to GP," Rahul said, recalling the moment when he was struck on the pads and given not out, only for New Zealand to decide against reviewing the umpire's decision.At the Basin Reserve, Rahul featured in three significant partnerships that have put India in a strong position in the Test match. His arm is still sore from the blow he took, but after months of preparation and homework delivering the desired results, he will have little trouble getting a comfortable night's sleep.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England eclipse India’s MCG record as Harry Brook’s fireworks power them to new T20I high vs Australia
articles.summary: England created history at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, surpassing India’s record to post the highest-ever T20I total at the venue, reaching 187/9
articles.body: England created history at the Melbourne Cricket Ground, surpassing India’s record to post the highest-ever T20I total at the venue, reaching 187/9 against Australia in the first match of the series on Saturday.The visitors bettered India’s previous record of 186 against Zimbabwe in the 2022 T20 World Cup. The 187/9 is also England’s third-highest T20I total in Australia, behind their 208/6 in Perth in 2022 and 200/9 in Hobart in 2014. Those remain the only two occasions on which England have scored 200 or more in a T20I Down Under.Brook leads England’s charge after early reprievesEngland’s innings had a dramatic start, with Australia’s Xavier Bartlett dismissing Phil Salt off the first ball. However, the hosts’ fielding let them down badly, dropping six catches, including three in the first three overs.Harry Brook and Aneurin Donald both benefited from the reprieves. Donald eventually fell attempting to go over the top against Edwards, but Brook made Australia pay for their lapses.The England captain smashed three consecutive sixes off Meredith on his way to a blistering 50 off just 20 balls. England raced to 74 in the powerplay despite losing both openers.Brook and Tom Banton then added 97 runs for the third wicket in just 41 deliveries. Nikhil Chaudhary eventually dismissed Brook for 65, while debutant Lachlan Shaw produced a stunning catch at deep mid-wicket to send Banton back.Australia pulled things back with three wickets in 13 balls, reducing England to 123/5 in the 12th over. Late contributions from Jordon Cox and Liam Dawson, however, helped the visitors reach a record 187/9.Brook backs England to defend the totalSpeaking at the innings break, Brook felt England had posted a competitive score and hoped his side could exploit the ground's dimensions.“Yeah, it feels like a good wicket. Hopefully we can use the dimensions to our advantage in the second half now. Feel like we've got a decent score. If we execute well, we'll be in a good position,” he said.Explaining his approach against the Australian bowlers, Brook added: “Yeah, I move around a lot and that's mainly to try and put the bowlers off. But yeah, I'm still trying to play the ball on instinct.”Australia's six dropped catches equalled their joint-most in a T20I innings, matching their tally against Scotland at Gros Islet during the 2024 T20 World Cup. Despite the fielding errors, the hosts will back themselves to chase down the target at the MCG.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Karnataka stun defending champions Railways in last-ball thriller to win maiden Women's T20 Trophy
articles.summary: BENGALURU: A target of 150 for a star-studded Railways side may have seemed a straightforward chase. But Karnataka had other ideas.
articles.body: BENGALURU: A target of 150 for a star-studded Railways side may have seemed a straightforward chase. But Karnataka had other ideas.Producing a spirited all-round performance, the Shubha Sateesh-led team stunned the defending champions in a last-ball thriller to clinch their maiden BCCI Women’s T20 Trophy title with a three-run victory at the Narendra Modi Stadium B ground in Ahmedabad on Friday.The triumph was the culmination of a consistent campaign, with the defeat to Delhi in their final Super 8 fixture being the only blemish in Karnataka’s run.Put in to bat, Karnataka, who made their only other final appearance in the 2018-19 season, made a brisk start, reaching 54/2 at the end of the powerplay. Opener Shubha stitched together a crucial 43-run partnership with the in-form Niki Prasad (28). The skipper led from the front with a composed 39-ball 48, an innings that proved decisive in taking Karnataka to 149/8. Railways fought back through their bowlers, with Poonam Yadav (3/18) and Sneh Rana (2/20) keeping things tight in the latter stages.Defending the total, Karnataka made a disciplined start. Monica Patil conceded just six runs in her first two overs and also provided the breakthrough, dismissing the dangerous Sneh Rana after being hit for two successive boundaries.Back-to-back wickets in the eighth and ninth overs further pegged Railways back, leaving them at 61/3 at the halfway stage.Karnataka sensed an opening when BG Tejashwini dismissed Minnu Mani in the 16th over. The leg-spinner returned in the 18th over to turn the match decisively in Karnataka’s favour, accounting for Kaushalya Choudhary before bowling Arushi Goel.With 18 runs to defend in the final over, Shubha turned to the experience of seasoned spinner Rajeshwari Gayakwad. The left-arm spinner held her nerve to seal a memorable victory and spark celebrations in the Karnataka camp.“I’m absolutely speechless. This was a win we have manifested for a long time. We had a balanced side, which stuck together and believed we could win through consistency and teamwork,” an elated Shubha told TOI.Crediting head coach SN Ameet for the team's success, she added: “He, along with the entire support staff, have been amazing and worked tirelessly behind the scenes. I feel this is the beginning of a great journey for Karnataka cricket. Today, we deserved to win.”Shubha also credited the KSCA Maharani Trophy T20 tournament, which was played under lights at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium for the first time, for preparing the team for the challenge.“The Maharani Trophy gave us a lot of exposure and helped us deal with pressure. A lot of credit goes to the KSCA management and the selectors,” she said.KSCA president Venkatesh Prasad hailed the achievement, underlining the importance of providing a competitive platform for women cricketers. “It is a phenomenal achievement for women’s cricket in Karnataka. This win shows that when players are given a good platform like the Maharani Trophy, it is only a matter of time before results follow. Sujith Somasundar, Kalpana Venkatachar, the selectors and the coaching staff have done a tremendous job,” he said.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sandpaper scandal: Darren Lehmann again denies knowing of plot while Australia coach
articles.summary: Former Australia coach Darren Lehmann says he and his staff did not encourage players to use sandpaper on the ball in 2018 despite detailed claims by Cameron Bancroft.
articles.body:
Former Australia coach Darren Lehmann has again vehemently denied any knowledge of the sandpaper plot, despite detailed allegations from Cameron Bancroft.

In an ongoing row about the cheating scandal that took place in Australia's third Test against South Africa in 2018, Bancroft published a testimony running to more than 4,000 words in the West Australian newspaper on Wednesday.

At the same time, Lehmann was commentating on Australia's third one-day international against England, with Bancroft's account prompting him to leave the match early.

On Saturday, Lehmann returned to broadcast for the BBC and Australian network ABC on the first T20 international in Melbourne.

In an extended and emotional interview, addressing a range of Bancroft's claims, Lehmann said:

He "didn't know" sandpaper was used by his Australia team.

No coaches encouraged players to tamper with the ball before or during Australia's tour of South Africa in 2018.

He is "not sure" about a walkie-talkie conversation with 12th man Peter Handscomb, which Bancroft claimed was an instruction from Lehmann to remove the sandpaper from the field.

He resigned as Australia coach before he was sacked and did not sign a non-disclosure agreement.

The fallout from the sandpaper scandal took him to a "really dark place".

Cummins' Australia captaincy at a crossroads - Agnew

Bancroft sandpaper claims heap pressure on Cummins

Lehmann's renewed denial came on the same day Cricket Australia confirmed its "unanimous support" for Pat Cummins as Australia captain.

Earlier, Cummins' fellow fast bowler Josh Hazlewood said he would consider his international future if the captain was forced to stand down.

The debate about the sandpaper plot of 2018 was reopened two weeks ago by allegations in the autobiography of Usman Khawaja, who was part of the Australia team in Cape Town eight years ago.

Khawaja's assertions that the whole team knew and should have taken responsibility have been supported by David Warner, Chadd Sayers and Jon Holland, who were all on the tour.

Warner, former captain Steve Smith and Bancroft were the only players punished for the cheating plot. It was Bancroft's testimony that heaped pressure on Lehmann, Cummins and the other members of the Australia team who played at Newlands.

Cummins, Hazlewood and the rest of the Australia bowlers who played in Cape Town have always denied knowledge or involvement in the plan to use sandpaper on the ball.

Lehmann resigned as coach in the immediate aftermath of the South Africa tour, but the former Australia batter has always maintained his innocence.

"Sandpaper, I didn't know," he said on Saturday. "Obviously, it was used.

"The biggest thing with ball-tampering is it was just a bad time. Everyone, we all made mistakes.

"But you've just got to try and move on. I know it's hard for everyone. The game of cricket is bigger than any individual team. We're custodians of the baggy green and we got a few things wrong."

Bancroft was caught on camera during the third Test, yet alleged the use of sandpaper had begun during the second Test.

In Cape Town, TV footage showed Bancroft hiding the sandpaper in his trousers. In his account, Bancroft alleged Lehmann immediately told Handscomb to "get the sandpaper off Bangers now".

Responding to that allegation, Lehmann said: "I'm not sure. That was all after the fact. It was already played out on TV.

"That's Cameron's take on it. I'm not going to talk about him, but my view is different."

In his version, Khawaja said players were encouraged before the South Africa series to get the ball swinging by any means necessary. Both Khawaja and Bancroft agreed players were further emboldened to cheat by coaches during the tour.

Bancroft elaborated further, saying the whole playing squad and coaches openly discussed and even celebrated the effect of sandpaper during the second Test.

Lehmann said: "No, I don't understand that statement as such, because at the end of the day, I didn't get that statement. I didn't get that question posed to me.

"I can't comment for anyone else. Again, because I said before, I can only comment on what I know."

Bancroft said the sandpaper idea was thought up by Warner at tea on the second day of the second Test.

Lehmann said: "I can't remember that conversation. Again, eight and a half years ago. You'd have to ask those people.

"That's the issue. I have my version and that's where I stand."

Lehmann is currently head coach of Northamptonshire. In 2020, two years after the sandpaper saga, he had heart bypass surgery after falling ill on his 50th birthday.

The sandpaper plot - who was there, who said what?

Cricket Australia sets up 'safe space' for players to share sandpapergate experiences

Lehmann was asked by ABC's Matt Clinch about the physical and mental toll of the sandpaper saga. The full answers are below:

I mean, I can tell you this. Eight and a half years ago, and I don't like talking about this sort of scenario, but I went to a really dark place. As dark a place as you can think about.

It took me, and this is just me, probably three or four years to actually get back to some sort of normality.

To the stage where we are now, I'm not going back to that. I'm trying to move forward. I'm not going back.

There's things I remember and don't remember. It's eight and a half years ago. It was a traumatic time, none more so for my family.

Without the support of family and friends back then, I don't know where I'd be.

And that's the same with the family and friends, and even Northamptonshire this year, who've been a second family over the last three or four years. They've been outstanding.

The support and messages I've got in the last few days have been something that's kept me reasonable.

I feel for everyone at the moment and their families. Social media has been so vitriolic. The hatred is there. It's just unbelievable.

I've never seen anything like it since 2018. And the trauma for everyone is there to see again.

For me, being one of them, you just try and contact as many people as you can, stay in touch with them and try and put one foot forward as best you can.

Eight and a half years ago it was terrible for a lot of people. So to revisit where we are now is not great for a lot of people. That's sad.

Clinch asked: "I don't want to ask you any inappropriate questions, but was that dark place a feeling of guilt over what you could have done differently?"

Could have done a lot of things differently.

I can only speak for me. I wish we did things differently and we didn't push the boundaries too far. We didn't get to the stage where we got to.

I've just got to take responsibility for that. That's where I'm at.

We're talking about people's livelihoods and how they can move forward mentally, physically, be happy again.

I want to see people be happy again. That doesn't look like we're there at the moment, does it?

Some of the things that are being said are just outright hurtful to a lot of people.

That's what I care about. I care about everyone. There's a lot of people being hurt at the moment and I think people have forgotten about that aspect.

Yes, there were mistakes. You apologise as best you can, you try and move on. That's sort of where I'm at, mate.

Again, I'm not going back to that place. I don't want to.

It feels like everyone's pushing you on to these bad places.

Some of my colleagues with ABC and some other friendly journalists have checked in, which I really appreciate.

But then you have people who haven't checked in who you thought would have. And then people making comments on you when they don't even know you for a start.

It hurts your families more. The families are the bigger picture in all this.

It's a big game and they do as many jobs as they can [unclear].

I think the way the team's evolved, and I think they've been to these press conferences and evolved, they're happy where they are and they've worked hard on everything to be the best they can be.

And that goes for a lot of people. That goes for me eight and a half years ago, that person I don't want to go back to, to this person now.

I hope people respect that as best they can. I hope you respect that.

I hope people can respect that everyone's going through a tough time and we just let the players play the game of cricket.

Because it's a wonderful game being played and I love seeing, walking around the parks and seeing the boys and girls trying to represent the baggy green.

articles.title: England in Australia: Nikhil Chaudhary stars as hosts win T20 series opener
articles.summary: Unlikely Australia international Nikhil Chaudhary rattles England and secures a tense and tetchy final-over victory in the first T20.
articles.body:
England 187-9 (20 overs): Brook 65 (28), Banton 39 (22); Chaudhary 2-21

Australia 191-7 (19.5 overs): Chaudhary 66 (38)

Unlikely Australia international Nikhil Chaudhary rattled England and was the match-winner in a tense and tetchy final-over victory in the first T20 international in Melbourne.

Born in Delhi and a team-mate of India captain Shubman Gill in Indian domestic cricket, Chaudhary only switched to representing Australia after the Covid pandemic meant he got stuck in Brisbane celebrating his 24th birthday.

Progression through Australian club and domestic cricket followed - plus a stint working in a Mexican restaurant - before the 30-year-old played his standout performance to date in his fourth international at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.

Helping restrict England to 187-9 despite Harry Brook's fireworks in smashing 65 off 28 balls, Chaudhary took 2-21 with his mystery spin and then hit 66 to steer Australia within 20 runs of victory.

The elegant right-hander appeared to anger both Liam Dawson and Sam Curran during his knock and the MCG crowd loudly booed England as the tourists slowed the game in the final moments.

"You always know it is going to be a big game against England so there is going to be some chirp," said Chaudhary.

Curran was left with 11 to defend from the last over but all-rounder Jack Edwards finished with 25 not out as Australia completed their highest chase on home soil with three wickets and one ball remaining.

The win offers some relief to Australia - an XI featuring a host of new faces putting aside the ongoing sandpaper scandal to take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series.

England can level the contest in Gold Coast on Tuesday.

Lehmann again denies knowing about sandpaper plot

After all of the off-field issues that have overshadowed this tour, this was a welcome entertaining game of cricket.

England lost Phil Salt to the first ball of the match and afterwards there was boundary-hitting, comically bad fielding by Australia, a bit of needle and a grandstand finish.

Chaudhary should take the headlines. After opener Jake Fraser-McGurk fell in the first over and Mitchell Marsh was sluggish in making 37, he found scoring more straightforward.

He repeatedly targeted the off side and, after Australia lost 3-13 from 143-3, he pressed on the accelerator by hitting Will Jacks for six and Jamie Overton for two fours.

The incidents with Dawson and Curran appeared innocuous but words were exchanged. The umpire intervened in the Curran spat to encourage Chaudhary to continue his innings.

By hitting Overton to deep square-leg at the end of the 18th over, he allowed England back into the game.

However, Edwards kept his nerve, while England also had to deal with Jacks having to leave the field with a cut hand after four balls of the penultimate over.

Chaudhary once said he switched allegiance to Australia because he feels "more close to Australian culture than Indian culture".

Fittingly then, he experienced the wild cheers of an MCG crowd after the winning runs were hit.

"My parents came over from India last night," he said. "It is their first game watching me as well."

Cummins' Australia captaincy at a crossroads - Agnew

When Brook had England 110-2 in the ninth over, the tourists looked on course for a score well over 200.

The four Australia wickets they took from the 16th over gave them a chance but it was their failure not to add another 15 or 20 runs earlier on that cost them.

England's skipper had a quiet ODI series with 23 runs across the three matches. Here he reaffirmed his position as one of the leading white-ball batters in the world.

He was dropped on two and three - both relatively straightforward chances among the six put down by Australia - but burst into life when hitting Riley Meredith for three consecutive sixes in the fourth over and was particularly destructive with his pull shot.

Brook's dismissal came when he tried to guide a cut off Chaudhary. Banton, who made 39 and shared a stand of 97 with Brook, followed in the next over and England never got going again.

After scoring 119 in the first 10 overs, they managed only 68 in the second, with Curran scoring 21 from 20, Jacks out for three and Jordan Cox never breaking free when making 27 from 20 balls.

With bowlers Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson and Sonny Baker now preparing for the Test series against South Africa, England need more from Curran and Jamie Overton, who took 1-37 and 1-44 respectively.

articles.body: The Sandpapergate controversy continues to haunt Australian cricket, with former coach Darren Lehmann once again insisting that he had no knowledge of the ball-tampering plot during the 2018 South Africa tour. Acknowledging that the scandal was a dark chapter for everyone involved, Lehmann said he accepted responsibility as coach but stood by his version of events.Speaking to ABC Radio ahead of the first T20I between Australia and England on Saturday, Lehmann said the controversy had taken a severe personal toll but maintained that his account had not changed."I haven't changed my views from what happened in 2018," Lehmann said. "It was a dark time, and we got a lot of things wrong, but my version still stays the same. It was just a bad time. We all made mistakes."The former Australia coach's comments come amid renewed scrutiny of the scandal following Usman Khawaja's claim that "all of us" knew about the ball-tampering plan and Cameron Bancroft's detailed account of the events in a 4,000-word article.ALSO READ: Sandpapergate fallout: Usman Khawaja, David Warner pulled from commentary duties amid fresh stormLehmann denies knowledge of sandpaper discussionsBancroft had claimed that conversations about getting the ball to reverse swing took place in the dressing room, with bowling coach David Saker and Lehmann present."A conversation developed in the changing rooms about getting the ball to reverse swing," Bancroft wrote. "I remember bowling coach David Saker being involved in those conversations. Coach Darren Lehmann was also present."The former Australia opener also alleged that David Warner "raised the possibility of using sandpaper to roughen one side of the ball".However, Lehmann said he could not recall being part of that particular discussion."I can't remember being present in that conversation," he said. "But again, it is eight and a half years ago; you'll have to ask those people. That's the issue, I have my version, and that's where I stand."Lehmann also reflected on the distinction between conventional ball maintenance and what happened during the 2018 scandal."With reverse swing, you throw it into the dirt, you rough up one side of the ball, you might pick at it; that's been happening for 100 years," he said. "In 2018, it went too far, and I'm (responsible) for that as the coach."'I went to a really dark place'Lehmann, who resigned as Australia's coach in the aftermath of the scandal, said he paid a heavy personal price and apologised for what happened."People said I didn't lose anything. I actually lost the best job in the world, and I'm sorry for that, and I'm sorry for what happened. That's all I can say to the general public," he said.He also opened up about the emotional toll of the episode and the years it took him to recover."I went to a really dark place. I went to as dark a place as you can think about. It took me probably three to four years to actually get back to some sort of normality," he added.The former coach made it clear that he did not want to revisit that period."I'm not going back to that dark place. I'm trying to move forward. I'm not going back. There are things I remember and not remember. It is eight and a half years ago; it was a traumatic time. I don't want to go back to that dark place, and I hope no one does. I feel for everyone and their families."Lehmann said he had "empathy" for Bancroft and everyone involved in the scandal, while criticising the hurt caused by the renewed media coverage."Some of the things that have been said are just outright hurtful to a lot of people. That's what I care about," he said. There are a lot of people being hurt at the moment, and I think people have forgotten about that aspect. Yes, we made mistakes, we apologise as best we can, and you try and move on."I'm not going back to that place … but it feels like everyone is pushing everyone to these bad places," he added.Lehmann questions claims about dressing-room meetingsLehmann also said he could not recall whether there had been a meeting in which someone raised concerns about the use of the object."Everyone talks about meetings at the moment; there (were) a whole heap of different meetings," he said. "There are conversations going on and some people are privy to them, and some people are not. I'm not privy to every conversation or meeting.”"So a lot of different conversations happen all the time, different meetings, not altogether; that's how it is," he added.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. His innings proved crucial in Australia's successful chase of 188.The 30-year-old had also made an impact with the ball, claiming two wickets for just 21 runs in his four overs. He dismissed England captain Harry Brook, who top-scored with an explosive 65 off 28 deliveries, and Sam Curran, who contributed 21.Earlier, England posted 187/9 in their 20 overs after being asked to bat. Brook and Tom Banton, who scored 39, helped the visitors recover from an early setback and build a competitive total.Jordan Cox added 27, while Liam Dawson chipped in with 17. For Australia, Jack Edwards picked up two wickets, while Joel Davies, Riley Meredith, Ben Dwarshuis and Adam Zampa claimed one each.Australia seal thrilling three-wicket victoryIn reply, Australia got off to a shaky start after Jake Fraser-McGurk was dismissed for one, but Sam Harper (32) and captain Mitchell Marsh (37) steadied the innings.Chaudhary then took charge with his aggressive strokeplay, forming an important partnership with Tim David, who scored 20. After his dismissal for 66, Jack Edwards remained unbeaten on 25 to guide Australia home.The hosts eventually reached 191/7 in 19.5 overs, securing a three-wicket victory with one ball remaining. articles.title: Nikhil Chaudhary shines as Australia beat England in thrilling first T20I to take 1-0 lead
articles.summary: Nikhil Chaudhary produced a memorable all-round performance as Australia edged past England in a thrilling final-over finish in the opening T20I at the
articles.body: Nikhil Chaudhary produced a memorable all-round performance as Australia edged past England in a thrilling final-over finish in the opening T20I at the MCG to take a 1-0 lead in the series.Chasing 188 for victory, Australia held their nerve despite losing wickets at regular intervals, with Chaudhary and Jack Edwards playing decisive roles in getting the hosts across the line.Australia suffered an early setback when Jake Fraser-McGurk departed for just one in the opening over. However, debutant Sam Harper provided an immediate spark, smashing 32 off just 15 deliveries to give the hosts a flying start in the powerplay.Captain Mitchell Marsh contributed 37 off 32 balls but struggled to maintain the scoring momentum as England attempted to claw their way back into the contest.With wickets falling at the other end, Chaudhary took charge of the chase. He first stitched together a valuable 42-run stand with Marsh before combining with Tim David, who scored 20 off 13 deliveries. The duo added 48 runs in just 29 balls to keep Australia firmly on course.Chaudhary continued to find the boundaries and hold the innings together, but his dismissal brought pressure on the hosts. With 11 runs required from the final over, Sam Curran was handed the responsibility of defending the target.However, Edwards wasted little time in turning the contest in Australia's favour. Curran began the over with a loose delivery down the leg side, which Edwards dispatched over deep backward square leg for a six. The crucial blow eased the pressure, and Edwards went on to guide Australia home in the final over.Chaudhary's contribution with the ball earlier in the match, followed by his crucial knock in the chase, earned him the Player of the Match award.Earlier, England had posted 187/9 after being put in to bat, with captain Harry Brook leading the charge through a blistering 65 off just 20 deliveries.Australia made an ideal start as Xavier Bartlett dismissed Phil Salt with the very first delivery of the innings. However, the visitors recovered quickly, aided by a series of fielding lapses from the hosts, who dropped six catches, including three in the first three overs.Brook made Australia pay for those missed opportunities, launching a fierce counterattack. He hammered three successive sixes off Riley Meredith and raced to his half-century in just 20 balls.England reached 74 in the powerplay despite losing both openers. Brook and Tom Banton then took the attack to the Australian bowlers, adding 97 runs for the third wicket in just 41 deliveries.Chaudhary eventually broke the partnership by dismissing Brook, while debutant Lachlan Shaw pulled off a spectacular catch at deep mid-wicket to send Banton back to the pavilion. Australia then struck three times in 13 deliveries to leave England reeling at 123/5 in the 12th over.Late hitting from Jordan Cox and Liam Dawson helped England recover and take their total to 187/9.Despite their six dropped catches, Australia managed to restrict England to a target they ultimately chased down to take the series lead.The result also extended Australia's perfect T20I record against England at the MCG. The hosts have now won all four T20Is against England at the venue, while England's only T20I victory at the ground came against Pakistan in the 2022 T20 World Cup final.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Pat Cummins to stay as Australia captain after ‘unanimous support’ amid Sandpapergate row
articles.summary: Cummins’ has been backed by the Cricket Australia board after a fortnight of claims and counter-claims concerning the ball tampering furore in 2018
articles.body:
Pat Cummins will hold on to his role as Australia captain despite the ongoing pressure of the sandpaper scandal , after receiving a show of "unanimous support" from Cricket Australia.

Cummins's future had become a topic of hot debate following a fortnight of claims and counter claims concerning the ball tampering furore of 2018.

His emphatic denials of any awareness of or involvement in the plot, which he shared in a strident 69-minute press conference in Sydney last week, contradicted testimony of several former teammates and raised questions over the seamer's leadership.

Usman Khawaja 's autobiography and an exhaustive written account from Cameron Bancroft alleged that the entire squad, as well as some members of the backroom staff, shared responsibility for Sandpapergate, with backing from former teammates, including David Warner and Chadd Sayers.

An independent forum was announced by CA in a bid to collate the experiences of all those involved in the South Africa tour eight years ago but before it has even begun, the governing body has made it clear that it stands firmly alongside Cummins.

And while that is unlikely to satisfy everybody – not least Khawaja, who saw his account branded "complete and utter nonsense" by his former skipper – it means Cummins can expect to lead the side again against New Zealand next month and can begin to plan for next summer's Ashes campaign in England.

A statement issued on Saturday read: "In the light of the ongoing speculation surrounding the Australian men's team tour of South Africa in 2018, the CA Board met to ensure measures are in place to protect the integrity of Australian Cricket and the welfare of all concerned.

"As part of this meeting, the board resolved to express its unanimous support for Pat Cummins as captain given ongoing speculation about his position."

Both Khawaja and Warner, meanwhile, were late omissions from the Fox television commentary roster having both been lined up to feature. With battle lines drawn, the momentum appears to be moving against them.

Cummins, who has seen his previous position as the golden boy of Australian sport challenged by negative headlines and reporters doorstepping him at home and training, said: "It meant a lot to speak with David and Todd on Friday. Being Australian captain carries with it an awesome responsibility. I have and never will take that lightly.

"David and Todd have a very tough job navigating cricket through all of this and I commend them for reaching out to me and to many of the players and staff from 2018.

"I support the forum 100 per cent. I will be there. All of the players and staff I have spoken with are very keen to go and to have their say. There will be a lot of difficult conversations but that is what's needed. Otherwise, from this point, captaining the Australian team in Perth will be my focus and priority."

Boon added: "We are absolutely determined to steward Australian cricket through this very difficult time with diligence and patience and to listen and learn.

"We've expressed our support to Pat and our concern for everyone impacted by the events of the 2018 tour of South Africa. We have learned from that experience and are proud of the team and the culture Pat and other leaders in the team have fostered over the past eight years and unequivocally reject any implication that Pat's integrity has been compromised."

Just hours earlier, fellow fast bowler Josh Hazlewood had broken cover by suggesting he may walk away from the team if Cummins was forced to step down.

"I think I'd have to be put in that position to make a decision, but you'd have to think about it, yeah," he told Code Sports.

"He's a great leader. If you went around and asked everyone in the team, you'd hear the same response. I think if we turned up for the first Test (against New Zealand next month) and he wasn't the captain and it was someone else, honestly, I don't know how that would go.

"It feels like it's been a bit of a pile on the last few days from different people. I want to back Pat and everything he said in his press conference last week, everything he's done for the last five or six years in particular as captain."

Reiterating his own stance, Hazlewood added: "Was I an architect in the plan to tamper with the ball with sandpaper? And was I aware (of) sandpaper or foreign substances being used on the field?

"The answer is no. When it boils down to it, I think those two points are crucial."

articles.title: Australia's Chaudhary downs England in tetchy first T20
articles.summary: Unlikely Australia international Nikhil Chaudhary rattles England and secures a tense and tetchy final-over victory in the first T20.
articles.body:
England 187-9 (20 overs): Brook 65 (28), Banton 39 (22); Chaudhary 2-21

Australia 191-7 (19.5 overs): Chaudhary 66 (38)

Unlikely Australia international Nikhil Chaudhary rattled England and was the match-winner in a tense and tetchy final-over victory in the first T20 international in Melbourne.

Born in Delhi and a team-mate of India captain Shubman Gill in Indian domestic cricket, Chaudhary only switched to representing Australia after the Covid pandemic meant he got stuck in Brisbane celebrating his 24th birthday.

Progression through Australian club and domestic cricket followed - plus a stint working in a Mexican restaurant - before the 30-year-old played his standout performance to date in his fourth international at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.

Helping restrict England to 187-9 despite Harry Brook's fireworks in smashing 65 off 28 balls, Chaudhary took 2-21 with his mystery spin and then hit 66 to steer Australia within 20 runs of victory.

The elegant right-hander appeared to anger both Liam Dawson and Sam Curran during his knock and the MCG crowd loudly booed England as the tourists slowed the game in the final moments.

"You always know it is going to be a big game against England so there is going to be some chirp," said Chaudhary.

Curran was left with 11 to defend from the last over but all-rounder Jack Edwards finished with 25 not out as Australia completed their highest chase on home soil with three wickets and one ball remaining.

The win offers some relief to Australia - an XI featuring a host of new faces putting aside the ongoing sandpaper scandal to take a 1-0 lead in the five-match series.

England can level the contest in Gold Coast on Tuesday.

After all of the off-field issues that have overshadowed this tour, this was a welcome entertaining game of cricket.

England lost Phil Salt to the first ball of the match and afterwards there was boundary-hitting, comically bad fielding by Australia, a bit of needle and a grandstand finish.

Chaudhary should take the headlines. After opener Jake Fraser-McGurk fell in the first over and Mitchell Marsh was sluggish in making 37, he found scoring more straightforward.

He repeatedly targeted the off side and, after Australia lost 3-13 from 143-3, he pressed on the accelerator by hitting Will Jacks for six and Jamie Overton for two fours.

The incidents with Dawson and Curran appeared innocuous but words were exchanged. The umpire intervened in the Curran spat to encourage Chaudhary to continue his innings.

By hitting Overton to deep square-leg at the end of the 18th over, he allowed England back into the game.

However, Edwards kept his nerve, while England also had to deal with Jacks having to leave the field with a cut hand after four balls of the penultimate over.

Chaudhary once said he switched allegiance to Australia because he feels "more close to Australian culture than Indian culture".

Fittingly then, he experienced the wild cheers of an MCG crowd after the winning runs were hit.

"My parents came over from India last night," he said. "It is their first game watching me as well."

When Brook had England 110-2 in the ninth over, the tourists looked on course for a score well over 200.

The four Australia wickets they took from the 16th over gave them a chance but it was their failure not to add another 15 or 20 runs earlier on that cost them.

England's skipper had a quiet ODI series with 23 runs across the three matches. Here he reaffirmed his position as one of the leading white-ball batters in the world.

He was dropped on two and three - both relatively straightforward chances among the six put down by Australia - but burst into life when hitting Riley Meredith for three consecutive sixes in the fourth over and was particularly destructive with his pull shot.

Brook's dismissal came when he tried to guide a cut off Chaudhary. Banton, who made 39 and shared a stand of 97 with Brook, followed in the next over and England never got going again.

After scoring 119 in the first 10 overs, they managed only 68 in the second, with Curran scoring 21 from 20, Jacks out for three and Jordan Cox never breaking free when making 27 from 20 balls.

With bowlers Jofra Archer, Gus Atkinson and Sonny Baker now preparing for the Test series against South Africa, England need more from Curran and Jamie Overton, who took 1-37 and 1-44 respectively.

articles.title: England call up Ben McKinney for South Africa tour after Jacob Bethell injury
articles.summary: England call up uncapped Durham opener Ben McKinney for the Test tour of South Africa after Jacob Bethell's injury withdrawal.
articles.body:
England have called up uncapped Durham opener Ben McKinney for their Test tour of South Africa as cover for injured batter Jacob Bethell.

The 22-year-old, a tall and attacking left-hander, has long been highly-rated by England and has now been rewarded with his first international call-up.

It leaves McKinney's Durham team-mate Emilio Gay, Ben Duckett and Jordan Cox set to continue as England's top three after relative success through the summer.

Bethell had been expected to rival Gay or Cox for a place in the top three before it was revealed he requires further surgery on a knee issue .

Bethell to have more surgery and out of SA tour

McKinney first caught the eye when scoring his maiden Durham century aged 19 in 2024 and that winter further displayed his talents by hitting 110 from 110 balls for England Lions against a strong Australia A side.

He has been name-checked by England's director of men's cricket Rob Key since and has been in a regular in England Lions squads.

Last summer, he scored 1,044 runs at an average of 52.20 in Division Two of the County Championship, where England's selector Marcus North also had first-hand experience of the batter in his previous role as Durham's director of cricket.

McKinney scored 145 from just 65 balls in a 50-over match for England Lions against West Indies A in St Kitts earlier this month and was already set to tour South Africa as part of the Lions squad.

Though sometimes loose outside off stump, his domestic centuries this season included 244 against Gloucestershire, 140 against Derbyshire and 184 against Middlesex.

At Durham, McKinney opens the batting with Gay at number three - an option for England if injury or loss of form means a change is required.

Their series against South Africa begins with the first Test in Johannesburg from 17 December.

articles.title: Ben McKinney earns England Test call up for South Africa series as Jacob Bethell's replacement
articles.summary: Uncapped Durham opener Ben McKinney replaces Jacob Bethell in England Test squad for South Africa after he was ruled out with a knee injury; England's white-ball side sweating on the fitness of Will Jacks after suffering a finger injury in their series-opening T20I defeat to Australia
articles.body:
McKinney, a 6ft 7in left-handed batter, has become a regular in the England Lions set-up and underlined his growing reputation on this month's tour of St Kitts, hitting 145 against West Indies A.

He will provide competition and cover for England's top order that includes county colleague Emilio Gay.

Bethell underwent a second bout of knee surgery on Thursday after being ruled out of the series due to an ongoing issue that also required an operation in the summer.

The 23-year-old had linked up with England's white-ball squad in Australia earlier this month, only for his anticipated comeback to be cut short by a flare-up of his knee injury.

England's the three-Test series in South Africa gets under way in Johannesburg on December 17.

Jacks an injury doubt for rest of white-ball series in Australia

Meanwhile, England's white-ball side could be scrambling to find a captain by the end of their Australia tour after Will Jacks suffered a bloody finger injury in the closing moments of their series-opening T20I loss in Melbourne on Saturday .

Jacks hade to leave the field in the penultimate over of the three-wicket defeat with blood streaming from his right hand following a painful attempted caught-and-bowled off Ben Dwarshuis.

Jacks had been set to captain England for the first time in the fifth and final T20 in Canberra, with regular white-ball skipper Harry Brook having brought forward his departure ahead of next month's Test tour of South Africa.

"I don't know [how bad it is],-he obviously came off with a lot of blood but I couldn't quite see what happened," Brook said of Jacks' funger after Saturday's loss at the MCG.

"Hopefully he is alright because he has been such a valuable player for us in the last two years. It would be sad to see him go home early.

"I've not even thought about that one [the captaincy] yet, that's a decision we'll have to discuss but I don't have an answer yet."

England's fixtures on tour of South Africa

December 17-21: first Test, Johannesburg
